Therefore, it is expedient that there should be a great and last sacrifice, and then shall there be, or it is expedient there should be, a stop to the shedding of blood; then shall the law of Moses be fulfilled; yea, it shall be all fulfilled, every jot and tittle, and none shall have passed away.
And behold, this is the whole meaning of the law, every whit pointing to that great and last sacrifice; and that great and last sacrifice will be the Son of God, yea, infinite and eternal.

The sacrifice offered for mankind by God via Christ must be infinite and eternal or else it could not satisfy justice. Somehow, these words apparently should clear up the confusion in how, although it is not just or well that the sins of a man be paid by any other than himself, it is just and well that an infinite and eternal sacrifice pay for such sins. Only an infinite atonement suffices for the sins of the world. Why? I’m not entirely sure. It is sensible to me that one cannot pay for the sins of another. But why then can an infinite sacrifice pay for the sins of another? Does not justice demand the debt to be paid by the person who committed the crime? Isn’t that the whole purpose of the punishment? Or is it merely a debt? I could see how if someone makes a mistake like breaking a window, where effects of the mistake are irrespective of the person who made the accident causing the damage—this case could be solved by any person who has sufficient means to mend the damage. But other cases such as murder have artificial effects enforced by man’s laws which seek to inflict a punishment or artificial justice upon he who committed the crime. This being so, only the murderer can pay the debt, for it was intended for him only, otherwise it is a useless and futile price to be paid and serves no one.

This could be a study question within itself: what sort of punishment or consequence does the atonement remedy? Is it God’s punishment? But why must artificial punishments ever be enforced? Could the universe provide its own laws for actions which leads to goodness, utility, and love when righteousness is followed and chaos and digression where it is not? But, apparently, God enforces additional consequences for unrighteousness. He is our parent. Parents often do this. They want us to learn.

But it seemed like God wasn’t merely teaching us as a parent when He banished us to becoming fallen man out of His presence when Adam and Eve fell. Was this to teach us or was this for some other reason? When Adam and Eve fell, or partook of the fruit of knowledge of good and evil, they somehow learned something and became something different. But it seemed God had to cast them out of His presence. The reason I say this is because He suffered the greatest pain in remedying the effects of His judgements upon man by sacrificing His Only Begotten. This great cost leads me to believe that God had no other option than to judge man as He had.

In fine, God atoned for our sins to remedy an Eternal judgement which necessarily came upon us. Only an Eternal payment could be made. Mankind can only make such payments by eternally serving its end. We cannot create eternal means or currency. But, supposably God can.
Heleman 12:1

And thus we can behold how false, and also the unsteadiness of the hearts of the children of men; yea, we can see that the Lord in his great infinite goodness doth bless and prosper those who put their trust in him.
Again, God’s goodness is described as infinite.
Moroni 8:3

I am mindful of you always in my prayers, continually praying unto God the Father in the name of his Holy Child, Jesus, that he, through his infinite goodness and grace, will keep you through the endurance of faith on his name to the end.

Mormon adds to God’s infinite characteristics grace. God’s grace is infinite. What is God’s grace?—or what was it to Mormon? Moroni’s commentary inserted in the Jaredite record summary, namely at Ether 12, uses “grace” in a way implying that it is God’s favor, love, and salvation. It leads to meek men taking no advantage of weakness in the words of Moroni (Ether 12:26) and humble men having weak things becoming strong unto them (Ether 12:27). Chances are that Moroni and Mormon had a similar or identical conception of grace.

The apostles are gathered together in Judea somewhere and, at the third hour of the day, a great rushing wind comes, which was loud enough to arouse public attention. The apostles see divided tongues of fire come down out from heaven and come into their mouths. All a sudden, they can understand a diverse population around them as if they were all speaking one language. Peter lists several different languages or countries present whom they could understand.

Some people think they’re drunk and mock them. Peter reassures them that they aren’t drunk and reminds them it’s only the third hour of the day. He then says this is a fulfillment of the prophecy saying that old men will dream dreams and young men will see visions. Then he starts teaching about Jesus Christ and compares David’s psalm where he rejoices that God would not leave him in hell but would deliver him, saying that it was not lawful for Christ to remain in hell and God delivered him.
Apparently 3,000 people were baptized after being touched in their hearts by the Holy Ghost as Peter spoke.

Peter and John go to the temple at the ninth hour, which is the hour of prayer. There is a lame man who is at the Beautiful temple gate (the temple is named Beautiful). He’s been lame from birth. They look at him and he heeds them, expecting money for alms. Instead, Peter says, “Silver and gold have I none; but such as I have give I thee: In the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth rise up and walk.” Then he takes the man by the right hand and lifts him up. Upon this gesture, the man’s feet and ankle bones immediately receive strength.

This story makes me think of my life. I am the lame man who got so used to asking for and receiving alms, that I perhaps forgot that I was lame. I became content with my mediocre life and the suffering of my flesh that I looked to God and asked for petty alms when He told me, “No, but here’s what I can give you.” As He takes me hand and raises me up, healing my infirmities, spiritual and otherwise.

Peter then uses his opportunity with no shyness whatsoever to preach to the people and tell them exactly what happened. He tells them that the very Jesus Christ whom they rejected and crucified is the one who had given the miracle before their eyes. He takes no credit but gives it to Jesus. He preaches of Christ’s return.

Peter and John are taken and held by the rulers, elders, scribes, and Sadducees, and they ask them, “By what power, or by what name, have ye done this?” Peter answers ever-so boldly that the good deed was done by the power and name of Jesus Christ, who is the stone mentioned by Daniel which he suggests this high council set at nought but which will become the head and corner. He also says that salvation is ONLY through Jesus Christ and no other name.

The council is surprised at the boldness of Peter and note that he and John are unlearned and ignorant men and were with Jesus. The man whom Peter and John healed is with them so the council can’t refute the notable miracle. I think it’s cool that God chose his servants to be what the world called “unlearned and ignorant” people. God really doesn’t seem to respect the learned above any other. He is surely no respecter of persons in any way.

The elders sent out Peter and John and counsel among themselves what to do. They decide to command Peter and John not to preach Jesus anymore. Peter, not afraid of these guys, boldly tells them that it is better to follow God than them and that he will continue to praise the name of Jesus for the great works and things he has seen. He rejects their counsel. They again threaten him and tell him not to preach Jesus and send them away.

Peter and John go and join the other followers of Jesus and while they’re gathered in a house, after discussing what happened, the Holy Ghost is present and the house shakes and they prophecy to each other. They begin to have everything common among them. Follows of Christ are selling all they have and bring the money to the common group fund.

Is Hell a created place or punishment made by God? Or is it the naturally formed habitation of the wicked and evil? One of the descriptions in the Guide to the Scriptures says “...it is the permanent location of those who are not redeemed by the Atonement of Jesus Christ.” This is aptly put in terms familiar to my recent studies. Because the wicked “as though there was no redemption made” (Mosiah 16). Also, the sons of Perdition would fall into this unredeemed class of spirits or people.
1 Nephi 15:35

And there is a place prepared, yea, even that awful hell of which I have spoken, and the devil is the preparator of it; wherefore the final state of the souls of men is to dwell in the kingdom of God, or to be cast out because of that justice of which I have spoken.

This is interesting that it says Hell is a place prepared by the devil. Perhaps it is just because God cannot have unholy people or things dwell with Him under his dominion so He must cast them out. He does not concern Himself with that which is not His own and which has rejected Him. He let’s those things or spirits go as they will outside His presence. And, apparently, the devil is the supreme ruler of the kingdom outside of God’s dominion. That’s interesting. There is space within space which is the kingdom of Elohim, and outside of that kingdom He does not concern Himself, it seems. It really reminds me of D&C 88:36-39:

All kingdoms have a law given; And there are many kingdoms; for there is no space in the which there is no kingdom; and there is no kingdom in which there is no space, either a greater or a lesser kingdom. And unto every kingdom is given a law; and unto every law there are certain bounds also and conditions. All beings who abide not in those conditions are not justified.

I guess non-human lifeforms could develop and reign and live and do whatever they want, but the devil also reigns in this outer darkness which is outside God’s kingdom. Where is this kingdom? Where are we right now? We are surely still in God’s care. I don’t know though.
2 Nephi 2:29
...evil… giveth the spirit of the devil power to captivate, to bring you down to hell, that he may reign over you in his own kingdom.

Sounds like we don’t know much about them. Some traditions say there were 3 wise men and the eastern traditions suggest 12. Some, perhaps embellished, stories state that the 3 wise men were kings of Persia, Ethiopia, and India. I guess we just don’t know for sure. The record of Matthew states that there were “wise men”, he doesn’t give the number of them. I suppose that the number 3 comes from the 3 gifts given in homage to Jesus as an infant.

title: Dating of Christ’s Birth
metadata_raw: Dating the Birth of Jesus Christ, by Jeffrey R. Chadwick | #BirthOfChrist
refs_raw: Dating the Birth of Jesus Christ, by Jeffrey R. Chadwick

body.text: In contrast to the article I’m about to read, I recall that Elder David A. Bednar, in April 2014 General Conference stated, “We know by revelation that today is the actual and accurate date of the Savior’s birth.” This is in accordance with D&C 20:1, if taken with liberal interpretation to mean exactness where it’s not necessarily implied:

The rise of the Church of Christ in these last days, being one thousand eight hundred and thirty years since the coming of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ in the flesh, it being regularly organized and established agreeable to the laws of our country, by the will and commandments of God, in the fourth month, and on the sixth day of the month which is called April.
The Church was organized April 6th, 1838, but the verse only says that this is 1838 years from the birth of Christ, and I don’t think it necessarily demands such details to be taken as sole proof.
Additionally, James E. Talmage suggested the same date in Jesus The Christ.
Regardless, here’s what I read from the article referenced above.

What if the second coming will occur 33 or 34 years (the number of years Christ lived in mortality) plus 2,000 years from His birth? If He was born around 5 B.C., this would mean the second coming would be 2028 or 2029. Add a year to each of those if He was actually born in 4 B.C. This would be pretty soon.

According to , where a lot of research and corollaries with the Enoch Calendar have been made, it’s suggested that Christ was born the night before April 6th, 1 B.C., which would have been April 6th according to Jewish evening/day patterns, right? The author of the website suggests this as the birth of the Savior because it was the first day of a Great Year on the Enoch Calendar, which Great Year is equal to 364 years. Interestingly, 1820, the year of the first vision, is divisible by 364 because it too is the first day of a great year. It is 5 great years from the suggested birth of Christ (1820 / 364 = 5).
2 Timothy 2:15
Study to shew thyself approved unto God, a workman that needeth not to be ashamed, rightly dividing the word of truth.

I want to become more familiar with important scriptures that support my beliefs and can help others when known well. I want to have these scriptures on my mind continually. I’ll list out some situations or doctrines that I want to start with:
The importance of prophets
Amos 3:7
Surely the Lord God will do nothing, but he revealeth his secret unto his servants the prophets.

This shows that God won’t work unless He reveals His secret or works unto the prophets. He’s not going to do anything without telling them. This is important for things like that sealed portion translation someone claimed to bring about. For supporters of that translation to argue its authenticity, they first have to disqualify the prophet(s) of our church. This is no easy task seeing that these men are firm and steadfast and manifest disciples of God.
Not only are we assured of the importance of prophets, but also shown how God’s work will be known by His prophets.
Numbers 12:6
And he said, Hear now my words: If there be a prophet among you, I the Lord will make myself known unto him in a vision, and will speak unto him in a dream.
Prophets will have revelation from God in manifest ways. They’re ones who have visions, like Joseph Smith.
Romans 8:2-4 (NKJV)

For the law of the Spirit of life in Christ Jesus hath made me free from the law of sin and death. For what the law could not do, in that it was weak through the flesh, God sending his own Son in the likeness of sinful flesh, and for sin, condemned sin in the flesh: That the righteousness of the law might be fulfilled in us, who walk not after the flesh, but after the Spirit.

What is the law of the Spirit? How can I follow the Spirit and be justified while I cannot satisfy the law of the flesh and be justified against sin and death?—for I will not be justified by my own merit to avoid sin and death; and, as Paul said, “For the wages of sin is death” (Romans 6:23 NKJV).

...the law hath become dead unto us, and we are made alive in Christ because of our faith; yet we keep the law because of the commandments… we speak concerning the law that our children may know the deadness of the law; and they, by knowing the deadness of the law, may look forward unto that life which is in Christ, and know for what end the law was given. And after the law is fulfilled in Chris, that they need not harden their hearts against him when the law ought to be done away.
Alma 34:14
And behold, this is the whole meaning of the law, every whit pointing to that great and last sacrifice; and that great and last sacrifice will be the Son of God, yet, infinite and eternal.

The meaning of the law is the point to the sacrifice of Jesus. But the law also clearly shows us that by it, we can’t be justified. I’m a little confused as to what the law is and why it was given. It sounds like it’s talking about the law of Moses but sometimes it goes even farther than that. Is it just the commandments in general? And what is the law of the Spirit, then?

title: Sexual Relations in the Old Testament

body.text: I’ve been reading the Old Testament and have been curious at how it was so common for men to have sex with their concubines and maidservants besides their wives. I was wondering how this reconciles with our current laws from God about sexual relations.

Abraham had sexual relations with both Sarah and Hagar. Jacob had sexual relations with four women, two were his wives—Rachel and Leah, and Bilhah, Rachel’s handmaid, and Zilpah, Leah’s handmaid. How was it permissible to have sex with his wives’ handmaids? The narratives of the wife-sister situation with Abraham and Isaac make it seem even more promiscuous of a culture, one where a man will kill a woman’s husband so he can sleep with her or where he will take a man’s sister if she is unmarried to sleep with her; both of these are founded on a fear that God actually enforces punishments or plagues upon those who sleep with a married woman, like what happened with Pharoah (Genesis 12:10-20). King David had at least seven wives, although he was apparently chastised for adultery with Bathsheba.

I just read D&C 132 and it does clear up a lot of this. Supposedly, if God gives a man a virgin, through prophets or the law, such as Nathan did to David (except with Bathsheba), or as Abraham took Hagar by the law, then the man is justified and not in sin. But if a man takes a woman against the law or when God has not commanded it, both of which are in place today, then the man is not justified. Also, the purpose for polygamous relations is said to be to multiply and replenish righteous seed. It must be a means whereby God has multiplied a righteous man’s seed to bring forth His purposes.

It is a law that feels so foreign to us. I can’t say that I understand it totally and I could understand how a woman would feel unequal through this practice, but it surely was done in the past and has been commanded and justified by God.
It’s sort of like the Fermi Paradox, where are all the other Christians?—and where are their writings and scriptures?

For I command all men, both in the east and in the west, and in the north, and in the south, and in the islands of the sea, that they shall write the words which I speak unto them; for out of the books which shall be written I will judge the world, every man according to their works, according to that which is written. For behold, I shall speak unto the Jews and they shall write it; and I shall also speak unto the Nephites and they shall write it; and I shall also speak unto the other tribes of the house of Israel, which I have led away, and they shall write it; and I shall also speak unto all nations of the earth and they shall write it. And it shall come to pass that the Jews shall have the words of the Nephites, and the Nephites shall have the words of the Jews; and the Nephites and the Jews shall have the words of the lost tribes of Israel; and the lost tribes of Israel shall have the words of the Nephites and the Jews.

This scripture makes it sound like God has given more scripture than the Bible and The Book of Mormon. But where are they? Maybe we just don’t have the writings of the lost tribes yet because we haven’t found them and become one people with them yet. This sort of touches on the topic of the lost tribes that they still are lost. Some people talk about them as if the gathering of the lost tribes is an ongoing, casual effort to teach the gospel to the different known countries such as in Asia and Russia, etc. But this isn’t in accordance with the scriptures talking about how the lost tribes will come forth with their scripture and break forth the ice, etc.

And they who are in the north countries shall come in remembrance before the Lord; and their prophets shall hear his voice, and shall no longer stay themselves; and they shall smite the rocks, and the ice shall flow down at their presence. And an highway shall be cast up in the midst of the great deep. Their enemies shall become a prey unto them, and in the barren deserts there shall come forth pools of living water; and the parched ground shall no longer be a thirsty land. And they shall bring forth their rich treasures unto the children of Ephraim, my servants.
Regarding the section referenced in 2 Nephi 29 above, Elder Neal A. Maxwell said,

Lost books are among the treasures yet to come forth. Over twenty of these are mentioned in the existing scriptures. Perhaps most startling and voluminous will be the records of the lost tribes of Israel (see). We would not even know of the impending third witness for Christ except through the precious Book of Mormon, the second witness for Christ! This third set of sacred records will thus complete a triad of truth. Then, just as the Perfect Shepherd has said, ‘My word also shall be gathered in one’ (). There will be ‘one fold and one shepherd’ () in a welding together of all the Christian dispensations of human history (see)
(in Conference Report, Oct. 1986, 70; or).

So he does think the same way here, there are other records that we just don’t even know about, even a third witness of Christ. That’s really cool. I’d love to read these. How could a whole group of people—the lost tribes—be hid away from our knowledge? That’s crazy. Are they not going to reveal themselves to us until the millennium? I would be excited to know more about that. I wonder if the prophet knows more about it. D&C 133 says that they have their own prophets. This is an interesting topic.
Nephi says,

…ye must press forward with a steadfastness in Christ, having a perfect brightness of hope, and love of God and of all men. Wherefore, if ye shall press forward, feasting upon the word of Christ, and endure to the end, behold, thus saith the Father: Ye shall have eternal life. (2 Nephi 31:20)

Steadfastness is unwavering, sure, strong, confident. Having a perfect brightness of hope?—how do I get that? What is the hope in? Is this the hope that becomes an anchor to the soul that Moroni talks about in the book of Ether?
Romans 15:4
For whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning, that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.
This is helpful. I can have hope through patience and comfort of the scriptures.
The New Living Translation has the verse written quite differently:
Such things were written in the Scriptures long ago to teach us. And the Scriptures give us hope and encouragement as we wait patiently for God’s promises to be fulfilled.
The point is, the scriptures are a source of our hope for the future, for God’s promises. Some of these are salvation and resurrection and meeting God, I think.

title: God Using the Ugly to Make Beauty

body.text: I am repeatedly astounded by the ability of God to use the most ugly and treacherous things for His gain and the gain of His people.

I was reading the story of Sherem in Jacob 7. Surely, Sherem must have been the cause of much sadness and anxiety among the righteous. He led people away from Christ. It must have seemed like one of the worst things. But God uses Sherem’s case as a lesson for the good of His people. Sherem is struck down by the power of God and the people repent and have him as a testimony that Christ is true and that Jacob is a valid prophet. The very instrument of Satan becomes the victory of God. I guess it hasn’t changed from when God told the serpent “And I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed; it shall bruise thy head, and thou shalt bruise his heel” (Gen. 3:15). The very act when Satan thinks he’s bruising God’s heel, such as when Satan crucified the mortal Christ—he must have thought it was his biggest and best victory ever; Christ was paying the price for the sins of all mankind and setting the path for victory of death and hell for all mankind—perhaps God’s biggest victory for mankind. It’s just amazing that God turns the table so rightly. It’s like the perfect game of chess: a grandmaster of chess can not make anything of perfect circumstances, he can only exploit mistakes. That’s what God does, He exploits the mistakes and tragedies, as they seem, and turns it into His, and our, victory.
Ephesians 6:10-18

Finally, be strong in the Lord and in his mighty power. Put on the full armor of God, so that you can take your stand against the devil’s schemes. For our struggle is not against flesh and blood, but against the rulers, against the authorities, against the powers of this dark world and against the spiritual forces of evil in the heavenly realms. Therefore put on the full armor of God, so that when the day of evil comes, you may be able to stand your ground, and after you have done everything, to stand. Stand firm then, with the belt of truth buckled around your waist, with the breastplate of righteousness in place, and with your feet fitted with the readiness that comes from the gospel of peace. In addition to all this, take up the shield of faith, with which you can extinguish all the flaming arrows of the evil one. Take the helmet of salvation and the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God. And pray in the Spirit on all occasions with all kinds of prayers and requests. With this in mind, be alert and always keep on praying for all the Lord’s people.
The Belt of Truth
Loins Girded—be ready.
The Breastplate of Righteousness
Righteousness protects the vitals like your heart (desires) and your lungs (breath of life).
Sandals or Shoes
Stand in holy places.
Shield of Faith
Faith is a good defense against the dark and scary times.
Helmet of Salvation
God is our head and protection. His salvation is the grace we humbly must rely on. Our thinking is our doom without God.
Sword of the Spirit
The spirit is the discerner between right and wrong and guides us to cut through ambiguity and know the truth.

title: Joseph of Egypt; a Type of Christ

body.text: I know I’ve talked about this before a bit, but there are so many Old Testament stories that are parallels or symbols of Jesus Christ. Here are some cool ones, some borrowed from  site.
Joseph of Egypt
Jesus Christ
Given a new name from Pharaoh (who represented God) ‘Zaphenath–paneah’ which meant ‘revealer of mysteries’, signifying Joseph’s role.
Given a new name from Elohim ‘Jehovah’ and ‘Messiah’, meaning ‘God is Salvation’ and ‘Anointed One’, signifying Jesus’ role.
Was a shepherd.
Referred to as a shepherd.
The most-beloved of his father. (Gen. 37:3)
The most-beloved of His Father.
Jacob made Joseph a coat of many colors. (Gen. 37:3)
God bestowed the robes and authorities of the Holy Priesthood upon Jesus Christ, it is after His order. (2 Nephi 4:33)
Joseph told his father, “Here am I” (Gen. 37:13)
Jesus told his father, “Here am I” (Isaiah 6:8)
Betrayed by his own brethren.
Betrayed by His own brethren (the Jews)
Cast into a pit by his brethren.
Cast into the pit of death by his own brethren in being crucified.
Sold for twenty pieces of silver (Gen 37:28), which was the price of a slave back then by the idea of Judah.
Sold for thirty pieces of silver (Matt. 26:15) which was the price of a slave back then (Exodus 21:32) by Judas Iscariot (Judas is Greek for Judah).
Joseph’s coat of many colors was dipped in the blood of a goat (sacrificial offering) and presented to their father.
Jesus took upon him the blood of all, as a scapegoat, and presented Himself a worthy sacrifice before the Father.
Blessed and taught those with whom he was in prison.
Blessed and taught those in spirit prison.
Became a ruler, second to Pharaoh (representing God).
Became a ruler, on the right-hand of God.
Was recognized by his brothers as Joseph in glory.
Will be recognized by the Jews, His brethren, in His coming glory.
Joseph’s brothers bowed to him according to his dreams he had as a boy (Gen. 43:26-28).
Every knee shall bow to Christ (D&C 76:110).
Joseph saved his family from the famine and death.
Jesus saves us from the spiritual famines and death.
Joseph returned his brothers’ offerings and payments for the grain he gave them as well as the grain they sought.
Jesus returns our offerings and graciously pays our debt. We are unprofitable servants before Him.
Joseph’s 12 brothers ate bread with him at the table of Pharaoh's house.
Jesus’ 12 apostles ate bread with him at the table of the “upper room” ()
Joseph returned in glory, riches, food, and gifts with his brothers to his father.
Jesus will return each of us to the Father in resurrected glory with gifts, tokens, the bread of life, etc.
Joseph gave lands of inheritance to his brothers.
Jesus gave lands of inheritance to His people.
Son of Jacob’s old age (Gen. 37:3).
“Shall grow up before him… like a root out of a dry ground” (Isa. 53:2).
Sent to by his father to check on his brothers (Gen. 37:14).
Sent by the Father, “I will send my beloved son” (Luke 20:13).
Stripped of his coat (Gen. 37:23).
Stripped of clothes (Matt. 27:28)
Raised out of the pit
Raised Himself from the dead
Promised deliverance to a captive in prison (Gen. 40:13).
“Today shalt thou be with me in paradise” (Luke 23:43).
Mosiah 3:19

For the natural man is an enemy to God, and has been from the fall of Adam, and will be, forever and ever, unless he yields to the enticings of the Holy Spirit, and putteth off the natural man and becometh a saint through the atonement of Christ the Lord, and becometh as a child, submissive, meek, humble, patient, full of love, willing to submit to all things which the Lord seeth fit to inflict upon him, even as a child doth submit to his father.
Mosiah 3:19 (rephrased)

Man, by nature, is an enemy to God, and has been since Adam’s fall, and will be forever, unless he surrenders to the persuasions and good offerings of the Holy Spirit, and abandons his interests in the natural man and becomes godly and holy through the atonement of the Lord Christ, and becomes like a child: humbly obedient, meek, patient, full of love, and willing to submit to all things the Lord sees fit to inflict upon him, just like a child submits to his father.

I remember on my mission we ran into a lady who was already christian and wanted to know if we thought she was saved. She asked, “Do you think I’m saved?” with a challenging tone. I told her “yes”, although I felt the answer required some context and elaboration. I was just thinking about that again. I was just reading this scripture:
Mosiah 3:20-21

…the time shall come when the knowledge of a Savior shall spread throughout every nation, kindred, tongue, and people. And behold, when that time cometh, none shall be found blameless before God, except it be little children, only through repentance and faith on the name of the Lord God Omnipotent.

That time could be now. The knowledge of the Savior is pretty widespread, especially in my country. So are none found blameless before God, besides little kids, except through repentance and faith? In this context, my answer to the lady in the situation above might have been first, “What do you mean ‘saved’? Saved from Hell, from death, from punishment of your sins, from responsibility to live a good life?” I expect she might have meant merely from Hell, but I would say, “Are you following God with your whole heart? Do you lie and cheat and do evil to people around you? Do you repent of your sins and have faith in Jesus Christ? How could I know these things about you? I’m not the judge of where you’re at so I cannot say. I can say that those who have faith in God and repent are saved.”

Then there would be some necessary follow up about how this is God’s true church and that by rejecting the information and scriptures we present, one would be cutting themselves off from God’s hand and blessings and knowledge He wishes to give. This is knowledge about Christ’s active and living work, about His personal church and visitation to mankind in these last days. It’s about additional scripture testifying of Him. Who would reject valid testimonies of Christ?

Some have suggested that when Jesus multiplied the 5 loaves of barley bread it was symbolic of how he transformed and improved upon the law of Moses (The Pentateuch, or first 5 books of the Old Testament), and that this new transformed and deeper or improved law was distributed by his apostles, or disciples. Further, Christ was giving the people bread, like how he said, “I am the Bread of life.”

title: A Mighty Change… No Disposition to Do Evil

body.text: Mosiah 5:2

And they all cried with one voice, saying: Yea, we believe all the words which thou hast spoken unto us; and also, we know of their surety and truth, because of the Spirit of the Lord Omnipotent, which has wrought a mighty change in us, or in our hearts, that we have no more disposition to do evil, but to do good continually.

Sometimes I, and surely others, see this life’s test as a struggle against sin. We expect it to be difficult and perhaps use the difficulty, or excuse the difficulty, as a measure of how much we think God is testing us. The point is, by this thinking, I consider temptations and desires for evil to be my own battle, something I have to work through myself—”it’s just part of life”, I say. But I don’t think God wants us to be struggling against temptation and evil desires. That’s miserable. I think the way to combat these things isn’t willpower or struggle of our own might, but working out the obtaining of God’s grace and transformation through God’s power. God can instill in us a change. This change can lead us to feeling free from evil desires—we won’t even want to sin. That’s the ideal objective, I think. That’s probably what it’s like for angels and resurrected saints. We should seek to obtain a change of heart and desire, not a battle of willpower and mental exertion against the dark forces. Let God plant in us godly desires and free us from the bondage of sin and desire toward it.

Role of stake and ward leaders in activation and retention
Missionaries are to join with ward missionaries “to teach again the first four lessons and to teach lesson 5.” (I don’t know why they didn’t just say teach the first five lessons…)

Apparently, after the merging of the Mulekites with the Nephites, the Nephites began using names that we also find in the Jaredite record. Perhaps there were Jaredites still living among the people of Zarahemla, but probably not. The record says that Coriantumr was the last among them, but he was found among the people of Zarahemla. Another theory is that idolatry of the Jaredites remained among the Nephites in cult practices and groups. Perhaps Alma the younger was involved with one of these, which could be what his “idolatry” referred to, and was the reason for naming one of his sons Corianton, a name seeming Jaredite in origin.

It’s also interesting that two of the three antichrists in the Book of Mormon (Korihor and Nehor) have Jaredite names. This could be owing to their chronological context rather than religious affiliations, but the theory is still present that perhaps they belonged to such Jaredite-derived cults of idol worship.

Give the people of Israel these instructions, which apply both to native Israelites and to the foreigners living in Israel. If any of them offer their children as a sacrifice to Molech, they must be put to death. The people of the community must stone them to death. I myself will turn against them and cut them off from the community, because they have defiled my sanctuary and brought shame on my holy name by offering their children to Molech. And if the people of the community ignore those who offer their children to Molech and refuse to execute them, 5I myself will turn against them and their families and will cut them off from the community. This will happen to all who commit spiritual prostitution by worshiping Molech.

This is an interesting term to describe the practice—spiritual prostitution. It’s as if we are supposed to have our supernatural and spiritual experiences only through God and no other medium (pun, sorry). If we do turn to another medium or idol or drug, we are being disloyal to God and trying to get what He can give us through another source.

But what spiritual or supernatural experiences does God want to give us? I think that we sometimes feel a void of the supernatural. God does want us to have this experience, we just don’t always get it like we expect. Maybe I’m speaking too much from my own experience.

title: The Liahona: The Word of God

body.text: Alma makes this analogy that the Liahona is like the word of God. It works by small means but if we’re slothful and don’t pay attention to it or if we ignore it, we’ll spend more time in the wilderness being lost and traveling in an indirect way. The way to travel directly to our destination of salvation and the promised land is to heed closely the word of God.
Alma 62:41

But behold, because of the exceedingly great length of the war between the Nephites and the Lamanites many had become hardened, because of the exceedingly great length of the war; and many were softened because of their afflictions, insomuch that they did humble themselves before God, even in the depth of humility.

This is the case with trials, they can leave you hardened and full of bitterness and anger, much like how the wilderness affected the children of Israel—they complained “what are we going to drink?” (Ex. 15:22-25; 17:1-4; Numbers 11:10-14), here, even Moses becomes hard and angry at the sore trials he bears. It seems that Moses was exhausted and sick and tired of the children of Israel and their whining and complaining and bad attitude in the wilderness. He seemed to even begin to resent his situation and address the Lord with his own complaining and whining and disobeys the Lord when the Lord tells him to speak to the rock instead of striking it for water.

Yet, on the other hand, trials can lead people to become humble and teachable. One instance of this is the poor Zoramites in Alma 32. They were so poor and perhaps even casted as a lowly group of people who were denied privileges like worshipping in the synagogue, even though they built it with their own hands. Yet, they were ready to receive the word that Alma taught while the rich Zoramites apparently were not.

Why is it that some turn out one way and others turn out another? One key element in the Book of Mormon is remembering what God has done. Nephi remembered how God had led the children of Israel out of the wilderness and parted the Red Sea. He remembered how God had blessed them and brought them to the promised land. He was faithful because he remembered. On the other hand, Laman and Lemuel forgot these things, or they ignored them. They complained, even after the encouragement of an angel, and seemed to have forgotten the Lord and His power and deliverance.

And the people of Nephi began to prosper again in the land, and began to multiply and to wax exceedingly strong again in the land. And they began to grow exceedingly rich. But notwithstanding their riches, or their strength, or their prosperity, they were not lifted up in the pride of their eyes; neither were they slow to remember the Lord their God; but they did humble themselves exceedingly before him. Yea, they did remember how great things the Lord had done for them, that he had delivered them from death, and from bonds, and from prisons, and from all manner of afflictions, and he had delivered them out of the hands of their enemies.
I don’t know exactly what the nature of sin was that the people committed that caused God to flood the earth. In Genesis 6:5-7, it gives some reason:
Genesis 6:5-7 (NLT)

The Lord observed the extent of human wickedness on the earth, and he saw that everything they thought or imagined was consistently and totally evil. So the Lord was sorry he had ever made them and put them on the earth. It broke his heart. And the Lord said, “I will wipe this human race I have created from the face of the earth. Yes, and I will destroy every living thing—all the people, the large animals, the small animals that scurry along the ground, and even the birds of the sky. I am sorry I ever made them.”
Later in verse 13, God says:
Genesis 6:13 (NLT)
“I have decided to destroy all living creatures, for they have filled the earth with violence. Yes, I will wipe them all out along with the earth!

So maybe a lot of the sin was violence. Also, the beginning of the chapter talks about how the sons of God had sex with whomever they wanted and this made God upset. God then decrees that the lifespan of mankind will only be 120 years.

Anyway, among the violence, it’s likely that sexual sin was rampant. In other places of scripture God condemns sexual sin, including homosexual relations and beastiality. After God destroys this wickedness from off the face of the earth via the flood, He says to Noah:
Genesis 9:17 (NLT)
Yes, this rainbow is the sign of the covenant I am confirming with all the creatures on earth.

The sign of the rainbow became the sign of God’s covenant to not flood the earth again. I heard a reference that is related to this that I thought was interesting, although I can’t say whether it is valid or not.

The symbol of homosexuals today, or gay pride, is the rainbow. People put rainbow flags up or put a rainbow in their profile picture and even businesses put it on their logos during gay pride month. The reference made is that perhaps Satan has designed this as the logo of homosexuals as an act of rebellion and disrespect to God, as if to say, “Ha, you see us sinning and doing whatever pleases our flesh and let us wave this sign of your covenant to not flood the earth again in your face.” This symbol of the rainbow could be an arrogant and prideful jab at God as if to say, “You can’t hurt us. You covenanted not to flood the earth again.”
This is a serious accusation so I must say I don’t know if this is true. Could just be speculation. But it does have enough sense in it to be valid.

I did a search of “three days” in the Book of Mormon after realizing that in 3 Nephi 8 - 11 there are a lot of repetitions of “three”, e.g., 3 Nephi 8:3—“three days”, 8:19—“three hours” (two times),  8:23—“three days”. There are many more, too. In 3 Nephi 11 the Father speaks three times before He is understood saying, “Behold my Beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased, in whom I have glorified my name—hear him.” (3 Nephi 11:7)
Here is a list of the uses of “three years/days/hours” in the Book of Mormon.

And it came to pass that they came forth, but were driven again; and they came the second time, and they were driven again the second time. And it came to pass that they came again the third time, and the battle became exceedingly sore.

There’s probably a lot to study here, but one thing I noticed is the three hours in the beginning and ending of Ether—Ether 2:14 and Ether 15:27. Maybe Moroni wrote the abridgement of the book of Ether as one giant chiasma. Surely Moroni knew about chiasmas with his father being Mormon. I’ll have to look into that more.
Alma 34:10

For it is expedient that there should be a great and last sacrifice; yea, not a sacrifice of man, neither of beast, neither of any manner of fowl; for it shall not be a human sacrifice; but it must be an infinite and eternal sacrifice.

This verse is interesting and I don’t think many people interpret it correctly, if I can assume that my interpretation is correct. My interpretation is that “infinite and eternal” describes here not the sacrifice but the Being who is sacrificing, i.e., humans can sacrifice a “man… beast… [or] fowl”, but only God, can sacrifice Himself, who is “infinite and eternal.” since God is both the sacrifice and the Being who is sacrificing (Himself), I suppose they describe Him both as the sacrificer and the Being who is sacrificing.
2 Nephi 9:7

Wherefore, it must needs be an infinite atonement—save it should be an infinite atonement this corruption could not put on incorruption. Wherefore, the first judgment which came upon man must needs have remained to an endless duration. And if so, this flesh must have laid down to rot and to crumble to its mother earth, to rise no more.

Here Jacob is teaching about the nature of the sacrifice which is the atonement. We learn from D&C 19 that “Eternal punishment is God’s punishment” (v. 11) and “Endless punishment is God’s punishment” (v. 12), because “Endless is [God’s] name” (v. 10). This would explain why the atonement, as described by Jacob (2 Ne. 9) and later by Amulek (Alma 34), is said to be “infinite” and “endless”. It is not a sacrifice of fowl or beast or man. It’s a sacrifice of a Divine, an Eternal. And it’s not being sacrificed by human, who can only sacrifice objects of equal or lesser status than himself—fowl, beast, other humans, etc—it’s being sacrificed by God Himself, the Eternal and Infinite.
2 Nephi 9:25

Wherefore, he has given a law; and where there is no law given there is no punishment; and where there is no punishment there is no condemnation; and where there is no condemnation the mercies of the Holy One of Israel have claim upon them, because of the atonement; for they are delivered by the power of him.
Romans 2:12
For as many as have sinned without law shall also perish without law: and as many as have sinned in the law shall be judged by the law;

These scriptures teach that if you don’t have the law, you don’t get judged or punished by the law. My question is ‘Why give the law to anyone if it only sets them up for the potential of getting punished?—wouldn’t it be better to spare everyone the punishment and just give no law unto anyone?
The following scripture expands the question and perhaps offers somewhat of an answer.
Heleman 7:23

For behold, thus saith the Lord: I will not show unto the wicked of my strength, to one more than the other, save it be unto those that repent of their sins, and hearken unto my words. Now therefore, I would that ye should behold, my brethren, that it shall be better for the Lamanites than for you except ye shall repent.

This teaches that only those who repent of their sins get to be shown God’s strength, in a good way, we presume. But it also expands the question by suggesting that it the heathen nations (Lamanites) are better off than God’s people unless God’s people repent.
The next scripture is my favorite answer. This is part of the Olive Leaf revelation, as it’s called.

And again, verily I say unto you, that which is governed by law is also preserved by law and perfected and sanctified by the same. That which breaketh a law, and abideth not by law, but seeketh to become a law unto itself, and willeth to abide in sin, and altogether abideth in sin, cannot be sanctified by law, neither by mercy, justice, nor judgment. Therefore, they must remain filthy still. All kingdoms have a law given; And there are many kingdoms; for there is no space in the which there is no kingdom; and there is no kingdom in which there is no space, either a greater or a lesser kingdom. And unto every kingdom is given a law; and unto every law there are certain bounds also and conditions. All beings who abide not in those conditions are not justified.

This teaches that only the things or beings which abide by the law by which they’re governed can be preserved, perfected, sanctified—via justice, mercy, or judgment, and do not become or remain filthy. If a thing or being abides not the law by which it is governed then it becomes filthy, whatever this may mean, and cannot be justified in the kingdom. I would think that such a thing must be cast out of that kingdom because it cannot abide the law of that kingdom.

And they who are not sanctified through the law which I have given unto you, even the law of Christ, must inherit a For he who is not able to abide the law of a celestial kingdom cannot abide a celestial glory. And he who cannot abide the law of a terrestrial kingdom cannot abide a terrestrial glory. And he who cannot abide the law of a telestial kingdom cannot abide a telestial glory; therefore he is not meet for a kingdom of glory. Therefore he must abide a kingdom which is not a kingdom of glory. And again, verily I say unto you, the earth abideth the law of a celestial kingdom, for it filleth the measure of its creation, and transgresseth not the law—Wherefore, it shall be sanctified; yea, notwithstanding it shall die, it shall be quickened again, and shall abide the power by which it is quickened, and the righteous shall inherit it.

These verses support my point. If you can’t abide the glory of a certain kingdom, you must go to a lower kingdom. This goes for people and even objects, like the earth. I would say inanimate objects but other scriptures make me wonder if any object is truly inanimate, especially spiritually speaking (Moses 7:48-50)

In Gospel Doctrine last week the teacher was talking about how women have the priesthood, or access to it. He was trying to praise women and compliment them, I think, but perhaps carried away to the point of teaching false doctrines about women and the priesthood. Maybe he was right how he worded it though.

In Women’s Conference 2019, President Nelson said, “Every woman and every man who makes covenants with God and keeps those covenants... has direct access to the power of God.” Also, “Those who are endowed in the house of the Lord receive a gift of God’s priesthood power by virtue of their covenant, along with a gift of knowledge to know how to draw upon that power.”

Does this second quote mean that every endowed member has a gift of priesthood power or a gift by virtue of priesthood power? Is the gift priesthood power or does it simply come from it? As he expounds it a bit farther in the next statement, I get the idea that the gift comes from the priesthood power of the endowment.

The heavens are just as open to women who are endowed with God’s power flowing from their priesthood covenants as they are to men who bear the priesthood. I pray that truth will register upon each of your hearts because I believe it will change your life. Sisters, you have the right to draw liberally upon the Savior’s power to help your family and others you love.
He goes on to clarify the point and I think it’s to the favor of my interpretation:

If you are endowed but not currently married to a man who bears the priesthood and someone says to you, “I’m sorry you don’t have the priesthood in your home,” please understand that that statement is incorrect. You may not have a priesthood bearer in your home, but you have received and made sacred covenants with God in His temple. From those covenants flows an endowment of His priesthood power upon you. And remember, if your husband should die, you would preside in your home.
So he’s saying that sisters have power from the priesthood in their lives and homes while they don’t actually hold the priesthood.

body.text: Gender can be a controversial topic in our culture today. The media is replete with complaints about toxic masculinity, which, from what I understand, is the belief that the expectations for males in our culture—being tough, leading the family, etc.—are harmful to men and society. Also are many movements encouraging women to abandon the traditional roles of women being mothers and wives and instead pursuing careers in fields that men have previously worked. They criticize the disparity in gender distribution in science and engineering jobs and some even blame men for this and many other things accusing men of being patriarchal tyrants.

To defend against some or all of these claims, modern politicians and thinkers who are purely secular in their interests and beliefs have to resort to logic and reasoning as their means of defense. One can argue on such grounds to a certain point, but it can be difficult to counter every claim. In fact, it seems that without a backing of religion and God, any argument to support objective morals and simple facts such as the importance and sanctity of biological sex, gender roles, etc., becomes near impossible. A system without God or religion in place seems only capable of totally supporting subjective morals and values, also known as moral relativism.
D. Todd Christofferson talks about this in his talk, :

Relativism means each person is his or her own highest authority. Of course, it is not just those who deny God that subscribe to this philosophy. Some who believe in God still believe that they themselves, individually, decide what is right and wrong. One young adult expressed it this way: “I don’t think I could say that Hinduism is wrong or Catholicism is wrong or being Episcopalian is wrong—I think it just depends on what you believe. … I don’t think that there’s a right and wrong.” Another, asked about the basis for his religious beliefs, replied, “Myself—it really comes down to that. I mean, how could there be authority to what you believe?”

To those who believe anything or everything could be true, the declaration of objective, fixed, and universal truth feels like coercion—“I shouldn’t be forced to believe something is true that I don’t like.” But that does not change reality. Resenting the law of gravity won’t keep a person from falling if he steps off a cliff. The same is true for eternal law and justice.

His words can be applied beyond their suggested application. God’s justice and laws entail also the ordained values and systems He has designed or created, such as family.  states, “Gender is an essential characteristic of individual premortal, mortal, and eternal identity and purpose.” This is a truth that can be derived by revealed religion, by God, but perhaps never by mere secular science as it exists among mankind today. The proclamation also spells out the ideal and sacred, God-ordained roles of men and women:

The family is ordained of God. Marriage between man and woman is essential to His eternal plan. Children are entitled to birth within the bonds of matrimony, and to be reared by a father and a mother who honor marital vows with complete fidelity. Happiness in family life is most likely to be achieved when founded upon the teachings of the Lord Jesus Christ. Successful marriages and families are established and maintained on principles of faith, prayer, repentance, forgiveness, respect, love, compassion, work, and wholesome recreational activities. By divine design, fathers are to preside over their families in love and righteousness and are responsible to provide the necessities of life and protection for their families. Mothers are primarily responsible for the nurture of their children. In these sacred responsibilities, fathers and mothers are obligated to help one another as equal partners.

Again, only a God-supported religion can really support these values. I love these values and my support is my belief in God and that these are His values and teachings. You can also get many more helpful teachings like, “As a parent, you have been given the tremendous responsibility of teaching your children to fulfill faithfully the roles of eternal mothers and fathers that the Lord has promised to those who are faithful.” This comes from .

It’s hard for the world to understand this by secular means, but the family consisting of a man, woman, and children, is the basic social unit of eternity and is the most effective way of raising children. Each sex contains important and unique abilities that support them in the positions of father and mother. Fathers protect, provide, and preside for or in the family.

Men tend to be stronger, faster, even more daring than women, which makes them more suitable and very capable of being protectors. Men also are made to be providers by way of their interests and abilities in fire, hunting, planting, cultivation, etc. Men are also incredible builders and inventors. We create and bring order to chaos.

Almost virtually every invention, building, and technology has been invented by men. Of course, as many might validly claim, women who might have contributed to this pool of accomplishments have been kept from doing so because of their roles as mothers and wives. This is an accurate suggestion. What I’m saying is not that women are incapable of comparable feats, but that men are very good at these and succeed in them. This ought not turn in to a competition where every praise I give to one sex is interpreted inveresly as an attack or criticism against the other sex.

Lastly for men, we are ordained to preside in our families in love and righteousness. To preside is to lead and be responsible for. There have been many wicked leaders in governments and families. Not all men have presided well and they will surely be held accountable to a high degree for any negligence or wickedness they brought upon their family. But the man is the steward of his home and family. He should work with his wife as an equal partner and counsel with her as they together raise their family. Any man who exercises unrighteous dominion or dominance over his wife and family is not following the God-designed structure of the family roles and will not see the success that God does in His family.

A righteous man who presides well over his family will make his wife feel loved and safe. She should feel safe and protected and supported by her husband. She should not feel the need to compete against him. If I were to spell out all the aspects of righteous precedence and godly masculinity it would take too much space. That should be done in another entry.

Women are primarily responsible for the nourishment of their children. Women have divine qualities of care, nurture, soft and healing touch. Women are blessed with qualities that allow them to nurse infants, even bear children via their womb, and patiently and lovingly teach young children to become capable and responsible adults. It should be noted too that parents teach and raise their children together, although this duty is the woman’s domain. She guides and directs this and does the brunt of the work.

title: What Does it Mean to Preside as a Patriarch?

A father is also to preside over his family. One who presides is one who takes responsibility for the outcome. A father doesn’t just take the lead; he is responsible for the welfare of his family and accepts that responsibility willingly and anxiously.

The man is the steward of the family. He takes the accountability for how the family is doing and God probably holds him responsible. Perhaps this is why the temple video used to have women covenant to men to keep the commandments and then men to God.

The observation has been made that the name SHEREM may not be Lehite. The argument goes something like this: The phrase, “there came a man among the people of” who “had a perfect knowledge of the language of the people” (, respectively), could be hinting that SHEREM had not lived among the prior to his appearance in, but had acquired a masterful knowledge of the language. This conjecture may or may not have merit. But if it does have merit, then searching for a Semitic root may be futile. The following discussion, however, assumes that SHEREM was a and therefore his name is Lehite.

This looks like a segholate form from the root *šrm. However, the root *šrm does not exist in north-west Semitic, including biblical (). It does exist in East Semitic (Babylonian and), šarāmu, and means “to cut out, to hack out,” and in Arabic, sarrama, “to cut in pieces.” It is possible that the root does exist in the Bible as a hapax legomenon in the ketiv reading of (, but verse 39 in the Tanach). There the meaning, reading with the ketiv, could be “the cut up/hacked up,” referring to the dead. But the qere reads šdm, a type of cultivated land or field.

On my mission I read Hebrews 11:1
Now faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen

and then I checked the Joseph Smith Translation, which only substitutes “assurance” for the word “substance”. It led me to thinking that faith occurred when you gained spiritual assurance for something you had previously hoped for. I even made a little equation for this:
Where , , and .
Now that I know a bit more about logic and functions and such, I would improve the equation to this:
Where  is a function giving assurance and  is a thing that is hoped for.
There’s a verse in the Book of Mormon that supports this understanding of faith.
Alma 58:11

Yea, and it came to pass that the Lord our God did visit us with assurances that he would deliver us; yea, insomuch that he did speak peace to our souls, and did grant unto us great faith, and did cause us that we should hope for our deliverance in him.

In the previous verse, the people had expressed a desire to God—”we did pour out our souls in prayer to God, that he would strengthen us and deliver us out of the hands of our enemies”; i.e., they hoped for deliverance. They then received assurance of this hope from God. This assurance returned great faith to the people. According to this, I can say that faith occurs when assurance from God is given for a thing hoped for. Without assurance, a hope is just a hope.

Now, I do have to add that both faith and charity seem to mean different things in different places of scripture. For example, hope can refer to a mere desire, or a brilliant spiritual knowledge that anchors the soul (Ether 12:4). Faith can seem to be fervent belief, or it can be a God-assured, hope-filled belief. I’m not sold on the idea that these words are used entirely consistently in scripture. But this doesn’t mean I don’t think studying their uses is beneficial. In fact, I think it’s great to study them out and find out what they mean in their context.
Lastly, I’m going to throw in a couple of other translations of Hebrews 11:1 to see if they shed any new light on the meaning of the words faith and hope.
Hebrews 11:1 (NLT)
Faith shows the reality of what we hope for; it is the evidence of things we cannot see.
Hebrews 11:1 (MSG)
The fundamental fact of existence is that this trust in God, this faith, is the firm foundation under everything that makes life worth living. It’s our handle on what we can’t see.
Hebrews 11:1 (DARBY)
Now faith is the substantiating of things hoped for, the conviction of things not seen.
Hebrews 11:1 (NKJV)
Now faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen
Hebrews 11:1 (NIV)
Now faith is confidence in what we hope for and assurance about what we do not see.

Almost all of these, besides the MSG version which is pretty paraphrased, suggest that faith is, or comes from, some kind of confidence or assurance of something that can’t be seen. These things we can’t see apparently can’t be proven or supported empirically. These are the types of things only spiritual means can prove.

A question not many have to wrestle with is whether to attend a gay wedding as a member of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. I have had to consider this since my sister has now had two gay weddings.

Initially, members must consider that even Jesus himself sat and ate with publicans and sinners (Mark 2:16). But also, Christ also said stand in holy places (D&C 87:8). The seventh question in the temple recommend interview is “Do you support or promote any teachings, practices, or doctrine contrary to those of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints?” Would going to a gay wedding be supporting or promoting a practice contrary to the church’s teachings? Because homosexual behavior is contrary to the teachings of the church.

After considering this and also asking myself, what would Jesus do if He were here? What would President Nelson do? I can’t imagine President Nelson attending a gay wedding. The gay wedding is a celebration of a gay union in marriage which goes contrary to church teachings and to God’s eternal plan. Families cannot be built or God’s plan succeed in gay marriages. Homosexual affection offends the Spirit, in my understanding. Homosexual behavior is an abomination according to the scriptures (Lev. 18-19, Romans 1) and has often been a wicked societies culminating sign of wickedness (Gen. 19, Judges 19).

So, while Jesus did eat with sinners and publicans, He didn’t put himself in a celebration of sin. In fact, it seems tacit that the sinners were sinners and that Jesus was teaching them truth. Attending a gay wedding doesn’t resemble this scenario at all. Are you teaching the gay sinners to mend their ways and preaching repentance to them? No.

The difficult part for many, and certainly me, is that attending a celebration of a marriage is a great way to show love and support for someone, whether they be a sibling, a son/daughter, or a friend. This is why many who are members choose to still attend the wedding or reception of a gay person. I however, decided not to for the reasons above. I don’t judge those who decide this, but I am satisfied with my decision and think that it is right, not just for me, but for all members who are trying to live the highest law. I don’t suggest that I am above all these people. There are many sins and many aspects of life. I have many weaknesses. I am just trying to do right where I can and I believe I have concluded rightly here.
Whenever the topic of contention comes up, I think of the words of Christ to the Nephites during His brief ministry among them,
3 Nephi 11:29

For verily, verily I say unto you, he that hath the spirit of contention is not of me, but is of the devil, who is the father of contention, and he stirreth up the hearts of men to contend with anger, one with another.
This clearly states that contention is of the devil and should not be had among the people of God.
, “Dissecting doctrine in a controversial way in order to draw attention to oneself is not pleasing to the Lord.”
The Webster’s 1828 dictionary has the following on contention:
CONTENTION, noun [Latin See Contend.]
1. Strife; struggle; a violent effort to obtain something, or to resist a person, claim or injury; contest; quarrel.
Multitudes lost their lives in a tumult raised by contention among the partizans of the several colors.
2. Strife in words or debate; quarrel; angry contest; controversy.
Avoid foolish questions, and genealogies, and contentions, and strivings about the law. Titus 3:9.
A fools lips enter into contention Proverbs 18:6.
3. Strife or endeavor to excel; emulation.
4. Eagerness; zeal; ardor; vehemence of endeavor.
This is an end worthy of our utmost contention to obtain.

I really like the first definition of “...a violent effort to obtain something, or to resist a person, claim or injury.” Contention seems to involve something violent, even if it’s through words. This means there is an attempt to force or harm. Although, I will say that some definitions of contention make me wonder how such a definition could be so strongly opposed by God, e.g., “To strive, or to strive against; to struggle in opposition.” I mean, we contend against the Devil and therefore have a contention against him. So I guess we have to interpret this in context when Jesus said things against contention. It seemed to mostly be in terms of doctrine.

title: The Natural Man is an Enemy to God

body.text: Mosiah 3:19

For the natural man is an enemy to God, and has been from the fall of Adam, and will be, forever and ever, unless he yields to the enticings of the Holy Spirit, and putteth off the natural man and becometh a saint through the atonement of Christ the Lord, and becometh as a child, submissive, meek, humble, patient, full of love, willing to submit to all things which the Lord seeth fit to inflict upon him, even as a child doth submit to his father.

Why is the natural man an enemy to God? And why is he stuck with this nature? Apparently, the fall of Adam is what brought this nemesis nature toward God. Why did the fall bring this upon us children of Adam?
Here are some of the possible effects of the Fall that could contribute to our natures becoming such:
Genesis 3:17-19 (NKJV)

Then to Adam He said, “Because you have heeded the voice of your wife, and have eaten from the tree of which I commanded you, saying, ‘You shall not eat of it’: “Cursed is the ground for your sake; In toil you shall eat of it all the days of your life. Both thorns and thistles it shall bring forth for you, and you shall eat the herb of the field. In the sweat of your face you shall eat bread till you return to the ground, for out of it you were taken; for dust you are, and to dust you shall return.”
Genesis 3:22 (NKJV)
Then the Lord God said, “Behold, the man has become like one of Us, to know good and evil. And now, lest he put out his hand and take also of the tree of life, and eat, and live forever”
Ether 3:2

O Lord, thou hast said that we must be encompassed about by the floods. Now behold, O Lord, and do not be angry with thy servant because of his weakness before thee; for we know that thou art holy and dwellest in the heavens, and that we are unworthy before thee; because of the fall our natures have become evil continually; nevertheless, O Lord, thou hast given us a commandment that we must call upon thee, that from thee we may receive according to our desires.
Building on this enemy to God idea, the following scripture attributes the enemy relationship with God to the world and friendliness thereof.
James 4:4
Ye adulterers and adulteresses, know ye not that the friendship of the world is enmity with God? whosoever therefore will be a friend of the world is the enemy of God.

With all these scriptures being mentioned, the only direct, named effect of the fall that I can think of as making our nature evil is a consequence of us knowing good and evil. The Ether 3:2 scripture is great, but it still doesn’t give the reason why our natures have become evil continually. It just says this is the case. Back to our knowledge of good and evil, how would that necessarily lead to an evil nature? We still had knowledge of good and evil in the pre-existence, yet we didn’t all become evil. Jesus had a knowledge of good and evil in this life yet he didn’t do evil. I wonder why it is that we became evil and enemies to God.
Mosiah 3:19 mentions what we must do to overcome this problem. Maybe this will yield some clues to why the problem exists in the first place.
●Yield to the enticings of the Holy Spirit
●[Put] off the natural man
●[Become] a saint through the atonement of Christ the Lord
●[Become] as a child, submissive, meek, humble, patient, full of love, willing to submit to all things which the Lord seeth fit to inflict upon [you]

How did the Fall make us not want to yield to the enticings of the Holy Spirit or be submissive, meek, humble, etc.? I still don’t know exactly. Why couldn’t Adam and Eve have eaten the fruit, gained knowledge of good and evil, and still be righteous.
An additional scripture I read that is relevant is
Mosiah 16:3

For they are carnal and devilish, and the devil has power over them; yea, even that old serpent that did beguile our first parents, which was the cause of their fall; which was the cause of all mankind becoming carnal, sensual, devilish, knowing evil from good, subjecting themselves to the devil.
The fall caused all mankind to become carnal, sensual, etc. I guess it doesn’t say why exactly, but it is the cause.
I just found another scripture which may answer this question:
Moses 5:13

And Satan came among them, saying: I am also a son of God; and he commanded them, saying: Believe it not; and they believed it not, and they loved Satan more than God. And men began from that time forth to be carnal, sensual, and devilish.

So this was the cause? This was the time when mankind became carnal, sensual, and devilish? Is it because they loved Satan and believed him? Believing Satan could be the cause of all of our carnality, sensuality, and devilish ways. He is the father of lies and inasmuch as we heed him, we are lost and subject unto him.
2 Nephi 9:8-9
…if the flesh should rise no more our spirits must become subject to that angel who fell from before the presence of the Eternal God, and became the devil, to rise no more.

And our spirits must have become like unto him, and we become devils, angels to a devil, to be shut out from the presence of our God, and to remain with the father of lies, in misery, like unto himself; yea, to that being who beguiled our first parents, who transformeth himself nigh unto an angel of light, and stirreth up the children of men unto secret combinations of murder and all manner of secret works of darkness.

For some reason, being mortal makes us subject or susceptible to Satan so that we enevitably become like him and since he “stirreth up the children of men unto secret combinations of murder and all manner of secret works of darkness”, we would do such wicked things.
This is a new question, why does subjection to the powers of death, or being mortal, make us susceptible to Satan? Why does a resurrected body not have this susceptibility?
1 Nephi 22:26

And because of the righteousness of his people, Satan has no power; wherefore, he cannot be loosed for the space of many years; for he hath no power over the hearts of the people, for they dwell in righteousness, and the Holy One of Israel reigneth.

title: Strong Men in The Book of Mormon

body.text: I noticed that Mormon uses the same phrase to describe the leader of the first leader of the expedition to the land of inheritance, which was followed by Zeniff’s expedition, as well as the description for Ammon, the leader of the search party searching for Zeniff’s people. The phrase is “a strong and mighty man.” That led me to search “mighty men” and similar terms in the Book of Mormon and I wonder what will turn up from it.

Strong men (Mosiah 7:2)
