The account in Helaman 5:41-49 is a story where wicked Lamanites have imprisoned righteous servants of God and starved them and intended to kill them. Through a turn of events, these wicked Lamanites end up having a heavenly manifestation where they hear God’s voice and then the heavens open and they see angels coming down and the angels minister to them.

Isn’t this story interesting? How can sinners who intended to kill servants of God have such a heavenly experience? I thought you had to earn heavenly experiences like this through righteousness. Of course, God does command them to repent and righteousness is important, but what God said before manifesting all these things was simply, “Peace, peace be unto you, because of your faith in my Well Beloved, who was from the foundation of the world.”
How often does God say something like this where He rewards faith and belief and doesn’t mention works? It seems that belief and faith are more fundamental at least if not more important.
Perhaps a question to study more in depth here could be: Does God care more about belief and faith or works?

Another question here is: In Helaman 5, the Lamanites have a miraculous manifestation of the heavens and “because of the greatness of the evidence which they had received”, “the more part of the Lamanites were convinced” and peace ensues. If such great good could be brought about by presenting evidence as such, why doesn’t God do the same today? Perhaps this consequence that ensued among the Lamanites had more to do with their state of readiness for the gospel, even though they had been very wicked—they were ready for conversion; because the Nephites, on the other hand, had the same account available to them and the same evidences yet they became “hardened and impenitent and grossly wicked, insomuch that they did reject the word of God and all the preaching and prophesying which did come among them.” (Helaman 6:2).
Later on we also get the people who have many signs and wonders shown unto them but it doesn’t lead to peace or conversion. They simply begin to dismiss the signs and wonders.

title: Keeping Commandments vs. Belief, Devotion, and Faith

body.text: Does Jesus indicate that living perfect lives is His desire for us or His expectation or are we mostly expected just to believe and give Him our hearts?
I guess this answers it:
3 Nephi 12:20

Therefore come unto me and be ye saved; for verily I say unto you, that except ye shall keep my commandments, which I have commanded you at this time, ye shall in no case enter into the kingdom of heaven.

I think the emphasis is just on believing and repenting because that’s the first step. But why is faith so important? Why can’t we just follow the commandments—keep all the rules? What good does faith do? Do we need to have faith because the motives and reasons of our spiritual devotion can only be supported by faith rather than empirical or other factors?
1.We know that prophets and apostles are fallible men, how do we both sustain them in their calling while discerning when they speak as a man without neglecting their prophetic roles?
a.Are prophets righteous? What’s up with Jonah?
2.Is everything that happens God’s will? Do things ever happen against His will? If so, why doesn’t He stop these things from happening?
3.How do you receive revelation from God on important questions or issues in your life? What does this process look like in practical terms?
My responses:

1.I feel comfortable with the idea of God using imperfect vessels to bring about His work. The problem here isn’t that God’s own prophets struggle with natural passions and weaknesses—the real problem is whether a prophet’s pride and ego could negatively interfere with their ability to lead us on the right path back to God. When perceiving error in a prophet or servant of God, we may question the correctness of their advice and supersede their judgment with our own. This undermines their authority to speak on behalf of God and pits our mind and will over theirs, or God’s.

So does this present a problem?—what about when prophets have been wrong about things they’ve said? I can’t think of any instance when heeding a prophet would have led anyone anywhere except toward God. One could make the case that such instances where a prophet’s endeavors or specultations failed or ended up being inaccurate are cases where people believed or heeded the prophets in vain. What about the Kirtland Safety Society? Saints were urged to support it and many lost money when it failed. If Joseph Smith was a prophet how could he lack foresight and ability to manage affairs concerning the money of the saints? Why would God allow such a thing to happen to the detriment of the saints?

Further, one could point to this instance and show that prophets, when not speaking about matters of salvation and morality, are speaking from their own mind and interests and that we should not be obliged to obey; for example, the Church urging members to be vaccinated. What if the Church’s advice to be vaccinated ended up with a detrimental outcome such as when the Church’s advice to invest in the KSS ended up with a detrimental outcome? What about such cases?

I believe that God loves obedience and a willing and humble heart. I think that God will take any opportunity to reward obedience when it is performed with the motivation of faith and love rather than fear and doubt—if we’re acting out of fear or using an opportunity of obedience to satisfy our doubt or prove a faithful idea wrong, we are in for pain and misery. But I believe that if we obey a prophet who asks us to do something trivial or something that ends up leaving us with a little less money or opportunity, as it seems to us at the moment, God will end up blessing us with more than we lost, if we did actually lose anything. We must learn exact obedience and use our minds and hearts to reconcile the difficulties we wrestle with somethings in such obedience; how did Abraham reconcile the difficult commandment he was given to offer his only son, Isaac?

title: Did Mormon Read the New Testament?

body.text: Mormon, the prophet-historian military-commander, sure seems to have read portions or all of the New Testament, especially the words of Paul. Some might accuse Joseph Smith of running out of fresh material and resorting to plagiarizing the New Testament but considering the amount of novel material in The Book of Mormon and the relatively few instances of New Testament scriptural overlap, I find that theory very unlikely. But the instances of New Testament reference made particularly by Mormon and not other Book of Mormon writers makes me wonder if he had access to the words he quoted. Mormon mentions that the three Nephite disciples who would never taste of death had ministered unto him, though Mormon wasn’t born until about 370 years after the coming of Christ (3 Nephi 28:26). Moroni states that not only did the disciples minister to his father, Mormon, but to him as well (Mormon 8:11).

My theory is that these three disciples gave the New Testament scriptures to Mormon and his son Moroni to read. Or, they delivered the themes and messages of many of the New Testament scriptures to Mormon and Moroni.
Here are the instances I’ve found where Mormon/Moroni cite New Testament scripture:

“But let him ask in faith, nothing wavering. For he that wavereth is like a wave of the sea driven with the wind and tossed.”

“And charity suffereth long, and is kind, and envieth not, and is not puffed up, seeketh not her own, is not easily provoked, thinketh no evil, and rejoiceth not in iniquity but rejoiceth in the truth, beareth all things, believeth all things, hopeth all things, endureth all things.

There are many many more but those are just a few to show the idea. Another idea that Bruce R. McConkie speculated was that Mormon and the New Testament authors could have been both quoting a common, ancient source of scripture.
Also see these articles discussing the same idea:

One other theory is that Joseph Smith’s translation of The Book of Mormon involved using words and phrases Joseph was familiar with, subconsciously or not, to piece together an acceptable translation. In this sense, it’s quite impressive that common phrases to him could come together to make such an intricate and well-made record. Even though there are many borrowed 7-word phrases between the Book of Mormon and the Bible, that doesn’t take away from the fact that The Book of Mormon is a piece of art and incredibly stable as a whole. Wouldn’t it be almost more impressive if J. K. Rowling had written the whole Harry Potter series using snippets around 7-10 words from magazines and such? I mean, it would still require incredible genius to build the story with such limitations. It wouldn't even necessarily be an advantage.

One reason why I think this theory is limited is because the Old and New testament references are respectively populated near the beginning and end of the Book of Mormon, making me think my original theory is more likely.

I’ve included the whole sections for further comparison but I am mainly interested in 2 Nephi 8:7. The discrepancy between Jacob’s version of Isaiah and the KJV Bible’s Isaiah “is my law” is replaced with “I have written”. Now look at some other scriptures and references I’ve found:
Proverbs 7:3
Bind them upon thy fingers, write them upon the table of thine heart.
Jeremiah 31:33

But this shall be the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel; After those days, saith the Lord, I will put my law in their inward parts, and write it in their hearts; and will be their God, and they shall be my people.
Romans 2:15
Which shew the work of the law written in their hearts, their conscience also bearing witness, and their thoughts the mean while accusing or else excusing one another;)
2 Corinthians 3:2-3

Ye are our epistle written in our hearts, known and read of all men: Forasmuch as ye are manifestly declared to be the epistle of Christ ministered by us, written not with ink, but with the Spirit of the living God; not in tables of stone, but in fleshy tables of the heart.
Hebrews 8:10

For this is the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel after those days, saith the Lord; I will put my laws into their mind, and write them in their hearts: and I will be to them a God, and they shall be to me a people:
Hear Him, by President Nelson

We wondered if a monument should be erected. But as we considered the unique historic and international impact of that First Vision, we felt impressed to create a monument not of granite or stone but of words—words of solemn and sacred proclamation—written, not to be carved in “tables of stone” but rather to be etched in the “fleshy tables” of our hearts.

The difference of our hearts not merely containing God’s word or law but to have it written in them is an important distinction. I suppose the origin of the idea of the law being written in our hearts probably came from Proverbs as that is the oldest reference. But perhaps the version of Isaiah that Jacob was using was more accurate as it clarified that the law is not merely in our hearts but is written in our hearts. I think this finding would be more substantial if the Proverbs reference didn’t exist but, since it does, the other Bible references to writing on hearts can be traced to the Proverbs reference.

And assuredly, as the Lord liveth, for the Lord God hath spoken it, and it is his eternal word, which cannot pass away, that they who are righteous shall be righteous still, and they who are filthy shall be filthy still; wherefore, they who are filthy are the devil and his angels; and they shall go away into everlasting fire, prepared for them; and their torment is as a lake of fire and brimstone, whose flame ascendeth up forever and ever and has no end….
And, in fine, wo unto all those who die in their sins; for they shall return to God, and behold his face, and remain in their sins.

So does this mean that repentance must result in changed behavior or else we will not be saved? What of the sins that we keep turning to? What about the parent who repeatedly repents of their unbridled anger or the man who repeatedly repents of his lust? What of the teenager who repeatedly repents of dishonesty? The list goes on. If we’re mortal, we’re going to be sinning, right? I don’t think these scriptures could be suggesting that repentance should lead to us living perfect lives in mortality? Maybe the degree of sin it’s referencing is more serious than the ones I’ve mentioned? Maybe I’m interpreting it incorrectly. But the question in my mind still stands: “Are you repenting if you’re not changing?”

After reading Romans 7 and 8 and the scripture in 2 Nephi 9:39—”...to be carnally-minded is death, and to be spiritually-minded is life eternal.”—I think that the goal of the gospel is not as much to change behavior as it is to change nature.
Consider Mosiah 3:19:

For the natural man is an enemy to God, and has been from the fall of Adam, and will be, forever and ever, unless he yields to the enticings of the Holy Spirit, and putteth off the natural man and becometh a saint through the atonement of Christ the Lord, and becometh as a child, submissive, meek, humble, patient, full of love, willing to submit to all things which the Lord seeth fit to inflict upon him, even as a child doth submit to his father.

Here it seems that the problem is not as much our actions—although those are end products that surely are still problems—but our nature. The fact that we lack submissiveness, meekness, etc. is the real problem. I suppose that’s why Christ said cleanse the inner vessel first (Alma 60:23; Matthew 23:25-26).
Ether 12:27

And if men come unto me I will show unto them their weakness. I give unto men weakness that they may be humble; and my grace is sufficient for all men that humble themselves before me; for if they humble themselves before me, and have faith in me, then will I make weak things become strong unto them.

Sometimes I’ve interpreted this scripture with taking weakness to mean sins we struggle with. The more I think about it the more I question this interpretation. I think God is talking about temporal weaknesses like Moses speech impediment, Moroni’s writing weakness, Pauls thorn in the flesh. Because, as Paul said, “[God’s] strength is made perfect in weakness” (2 Corinthians 12:9).
Paul also has words similar to the ones in Ether 12.
2 Corinthians 12:7

And lest I should be exalted above measure through the abundance of the revelations, there was given to me a thorn in the flesh, the messenger of Satan to buffet me, lest I should be exalted above measure.

This scripture expresses the same sentiment and may even be related from the same source as Moroni’s revelation contained in Ether 12. Importantly, though, in this scripture, the weakness Paul deals with is a “thorn in the flesh”. Note that it is an ailment of flesh and not spirit. I don’t think we could argue that God gives us spiritual weaknesses to make us humble. He may give us physical weaknesses, or at least allow them to persist with us, but God does not tempt us with spiritual weakness or immoral temptations.

With this being said, it may be true that if we come to God with our spiritual weaknesses or immoral imperfections that we can be made strong and our weakness can become strength, but I don’t think that’s what the scripture is trying to say in the case of Moroni or Paul.
Patriarchy as defined in our society is “a system of society where the men are the head-of-the-household, carry the most power and where the family lineage passes on through men.”

Is a patriarchal order divinely appointed? Is it the order of heaven? If it is the order of heaven and functions well there, does that mean it is the optimal and preferred system or order here on this fallen earth? These questions may be considered throughout this study as I identify different resources and points of view. I want to begin by suggesting that the systems and laws of the celestial kingdom may not be suitable for a fallen world or a government governing a group of individuals carrying diverse arrays of beliefs. When addressing what system of governing is best for a society as diverse as our country or world culture, we must admit that it won’t be a system which upholds morality and divine order as the celestial law does.

All kingdoms have a law given; And there are many kingdoms; for there is no space in the which there is no kingdom; and there is no kingdom in which there is no space, either a greater or a lesser kingdom. And unto every kingdom is given a law; and unto every law there are certain bounds also and conditions.

From this scripture I interpret that there are varying laws and conditions for varying spaces and kingdoms. This earth is in a low state of glory and thus may not be governed by a law suited for a kingdom of a high degree of glory.

I think it’s important to examine the scrutiny and criticism that patriarchy as demonstrated in our known earthly history has received. One venue that has directed much of this, and rightly so in some cases, has been feminism. Feminism has had changing objectives and methods during its existence and I will address the four waves of feminism that we’ve seen.
The waves of feminism

The first wave of feminism took place in the 19th and early 20th centuries. It resulted in securing voting rights and more equal property rights for women. The second wave pushed onto issues regarding domestic and sexual abuse, workplace sexism, sexual expression (pornography, etc.), and reproductive care (also including abortion). The objectives become more controversial here and the feminists within the movement become somewhat split. The controversy within feminism on whether pornography is good or bad for feminist intrests is known as the Sex Wars.  The third wave of feminism pursues topics of diversity, transfeminism, intersectionality—a topic similar to systemic theories which suggest combinations of race, class, gender, weight, etc. are subject to advantage or disadvantage in our society.
Patriarchy

First, let it be said that the world refers to patriarchy as a generic term encompassing domineering and wicked attitudes of unbridled men who exploit women, others, and the world without regard to individual consent or respect. This form of patriarchy allows for evil monarchical men to rule without accountability and to selfishly seek out their own desires as if such were all that truly mattered. This form of governance as described is evil. A system that allows one individual to pursue hedonistic and selfish ambitions at the expense of abusing and exploiting others is not godly but quite the opposite.

There is, however, a godly form of patriarchy that I want to discuss and, importantly, it is not a watered down version of patriarchy which some attempt to use as a means of mitigating political offense. This is the true and godly form of the patriarchal order which system rules the heavens and families built upon God’s true order and gospel. This godly form will be described in list form with sources attached.

Sexism
One question some might consider is whether patriarchal systems, or the Church which endorses such, are sexist.
Sexism
Prejudice, stereotyping, or discrimination, typically against women, on the basis of sex.
Prejudice
Preconceived opinion that is not based on reason or actual experience.
Stereotype
A widely held but fixed and oversimplified image or idea of a particular type of person or thing.
Discrimination
The unjust or prejudicial treatment of different categories of people or things, especially on the grounds of race, age, or sex.

Based on the definitions given above, is the Church and the patriarchal order sexist? In other words, is the patriarchal order implement prejudice, stereotyping, or discrimination against men or women?
Let’s look at each of these individually:
Prejudice

Does the patriarchal system or order as taught by the Church imply or entail preconceived opinions about men or women that are not based on reason or actual experience? The patriarchal system does entail expectations of gender roles including protecting, providing, and presiding for men, and for women to be the primary nurturers of their children. Men have a defined role of presidency in the family where the wife and children submit to their father who acts in love and righteousness. Are these opinions or ideas based on reason or actual experience? I would say that by virtue of the divinely given revelations they derive from, they are reasonably true to those in the Church. They are not based merely in tradition. But the world would probably define this as a traditional source rather than a reasonable source. To us, the patriarchal system is not prejudiced, to the world, it is.
Stereotype

Is the patriarchal system stereotyped? It does entail fixed and perhaps oversimplified ideas of a particular group or thing—gender roles. It does prescribe gender roles and imply that by virtue of these God-given roles, women and men possess inherent abilities and characteristics that allow them to effectively fulfill their roles; e.g., men possess superior stature, muscle, speed, and other skills to women that enable them to be, generally speaking, better protectors and providers in a world where such skills are needed for such tasks. Granted, the world we live in today does not favor such characteristics for hunting and protecting and men do not necessarily have any advantage because of such.

Providing for a family does not require great strength or hunting skills as it used to. Nor does protecting a family demand combative warrior skills as it used to. One could argue that in today’s world, a man is not better suited for protecting or providing for his family as he used to be. Regardless of the inherent skills expedient for these tasks, a man may very well thrive in achieving these feats more than a woman as they are his divinely appointed roles.

This is similar to a woman—a man can be just as available as a woman these days to nurture the children of his family. But it may be that a woman receives more meaning and fulfillment in pursuing this feat than a man. This is somewhat speculative but I think you could find substance to back it up.
These gender roles are conducive to happiness for both sexes and the whole family which endorse them.
So does the patriarchal system stereotype? Probably, yes.
Discrimination

Does the patriarchal system discriminate? The definition of discrimination asserts that the treatment concerned is unjust. Whether the treatment of each gender in a patriarchal system is just or not may depend upon who you ask but I would argue that when the patriarchal system is followed as prescribed by the church and scripture, the treatment of each gender is complementary, loving, respectful, and enabling. The father of the patriarchal system is not domineering, abusive, undermining, or belittling. He is meek, compassionate, righteous, etc. Because of this, I say that the patriarchal system as taught by the church is not discriminatory.

Overall, to the claim that the church’s prescription of the patriarchal order is sexist, I say that it is probably not. Perhaps you could claim that it is based on the stereotypes involved, but in that sense it’s only sexist in a watered-down and innocuous sort of way. It certainly is not sexist in any real or serious sense.

I think one of the main problems people have is that when there is any perceivable difference identified between races or sexes, our culture flips out in rage because I suppose they think difference means inequality and unfair treatment. Evidently, they cannot conceive of different and complementary roles yielding an equal and fair system.

In heaven, God rules as supreme monarch and leader and is acknowledged as such by all who live there and they give Him not only allegiance and submission, but also continuous praise (1 Nephi 1:8). This is the case yet I do not hear of any Christian complaining that God has the unfair benefit and advantage and that Heaven is not a fair place. What right does God have to the throne? Of course He is the rightful King and God.

An army commander or righteous political leader or king may exact respect for their following and this is not an unfair system—in fact these can all be incredibly successful systems. Just because the father is designed to preside in love and righteousness does not mean that the system is flawed or unfair. If anyone thinks its unfair that the man presides instead of the woman in God’s design for families then they don’t understand what it means to preside or they wrongly associate presidency with accolade and worldly praise. The father who presides in righteousness in his home does not merit any more tangible benefits to the woman.
President Benson’s talk

, by Ezra Taft Benson. This talk is pretty good. President Benson talks about the last days and how they are coming soon. It doesn’t really add much about the times of the Gentiles except what has been said in D&C 45.
The 201st year hinge point

201st year hinge point where Nephites began to be wicked. Same timeline at 2021 (4 Nephi 1:22-27). Elder Quentin L. Cook points out this possible applicable parallel between the Nephites and us today where the two hundred and first year after the coming of Christ among the Nephites, or the coming of Christ at the restoration in our case, marks a point of turning among the people where they begin to digress into wickedness.

And now, in this two hundred and first year there began to be among them those who were lifted up in pride, such as the wearing of costly apparel, and all manner of fine pearls, and of the fine things of the world.  And from that time forth they did have their goods and their substance no more common among them.
, Orson Pratt

The best thing for us to do is to depend upon what God reveals. If he gives us any knowledge regarding chronology, depend upon it; and he has given us a great deal of information with regard to the signs of the times. If he has not given us the age of the world, he has given us that whereby we may know that we live in the generation in which the times of the Gentiles will be fulfilled. D&C 45:25-31 JS—H 1:41 He informed us, in the rise of this Church, that that generation should not pass away until the times of the Gentiles should be fulfilled. D&C 45:25-31 D&C 88:84 And then we have other revelations, showing that when their times are fulfilled there is a speedy and short work Rom. 9:27-28 to be accomplished in the gathering of the house of Israel from the four quarters of the earth. 3 Ne. 16:5 Moses 7:62 They are to be brought out of all nations, kindreds, tongues, and people 2 Ne. 30:8 with a mighty hand and outstretched arm. Deut. 26:8 We are told that God will then perform wonders, miracles and signs, D&C 35:8-10 JS—M 1:22 greater than ever have been performed since the creation of the world; D&C 29:14 that he will bring back his covenant people. D&C 45:39-43 After the Jews have rebuilt Jerusalem, and after the Temple is erected, Joel 3:1-21 Zech. 12:1-14 the Lord Jesus will come. Zech. 14:1-21

Apparently, some of the early church members thought that the times of the Gentiles were fulfilled in their lifetimes which would yield a more speedy passing of events including the second coming of Christ, etc., right?
Orson Pratt referenced a lot of scriptures there, though. I want to bring up a few of them.

Therefore, tarry ye, and labor diligently, that you may be perfected in your ministry to go forth among the Gentiles for the last time, as many as the mouth of the Lord shall name, to bind up the law and seal up the testimony, and to prepare the saints for the hour of judgment which is to come;
Granted, this language does make it sound like it’s wrapping up sooner than I would have thought. For, for two hundred years nearly we’ve been going forth among the Gentiles for the last time.
Romans 9:27-28
27 Esaias also crieth concerning Israel, Though the number of the children of Israel be as the sand of the sea, a remnant shall be saved:
28 For he will finish the work, and cut it short in righteousness: because a short work will the Lord make upon the earth.
Orson Pratt interpreted this to mean that God’s work among the Gentiles during the last days would be short and speedy work. I guess it’s all relative. 200 years is short to God(?).
Moses 7:62

And righteousness will I send down out of heaven; and truth will I send forth out of the earth, to bear testimony of mine Only Begotten; his resurrection from the dead; yea, and also the resurrection of all men; and righteousness and truth will I cause to sweep the earth as with a flood, to gather out mine elect from the four quarters of the earth, unto a place which I shall prepare, an Holy City, that my people may gird up their loins, and be looking forth for the time of my coming; for there shall be my tabernacle, and it shall be called Zion, a New Jerusalem.

You could argue that these words talk about the restoration when Christ appeared in the Kirtland temple or in the Salt Lake temple. If that were the case, what do we make of things? Has Christ’s second coming already started?
8 And it shall come to pass that the Lord God shall commence his work among all nations, kindreds, tongues, and people, to bring about the restoration of his people upon the earth.

9 And with righteousness shall the Lord God judge the poor, and reprove with equity for the meek of the earth. And he shall smite the earth with the rod of his mouth; and with the breath of his lips shall he slay the wicked.

10 For the time speedily cometh that the Lord God shall cause a great division among the people, and the wicked will he destroy; and he will spare his people, yea, even if it so be that he must destroy the wicked by fire.
He says “speedily” but it seems to be less so than we would have thought. Unless that means that it will happen suddenly, not necessarily in a short amount of time.
3 Nephi, the fulness taken from the Gentiles
In 3 Nephi 16:10, what does it mean that the fullness of the gospel will be taken from the Gentiles?
Orsan Pratt has a quote on this from Gathering of Israel, Etc.

For twenty-seven years the Lord has been fulfilling this directly before the eyes of all this nation. Little did they think when they came upon us in Nauvoo, and drove us out from our homes and firesides and told us to flee away beyond this great chain of rocky mountains, that they were fulfilling this great prophecy uttered before this people had an existence. “I will bring the fulness of my gospel from among them;” 3 Ne. 16:10 and mark the next sentence—“and then I will remember my covenant.” 3 Ne. 16:11 When? When he gets the people out from the midst of this nation. “Then I will remember my covenant which I made unto my people, O house of Israel, and I will bring my gospel unto them.” 3 Ne. 16:11 Has it been fulfilled? Yes. It is over a quarter of a century since the Lord brought us out, and laid a foundation for us to live here; and we have been enabled by his power to erect towns villages and cities, to open up farms, and begin to live, and we have got a broad foundation laid; and now, the next thing is—“I will bring the fulness of my gospel unto thee, O house of Israel;” 3 Ne. 16:11 that is, unto the Indians; in other words—they shall come unto a knowledge of the fulness of my Gospel. 3 Ne. 16:12 “Yet if the Gentiles will repent and return unto me, saith the Father, behold they shall be numbered among my people, the house of Israel.” 3 Ne. 16:13.

This suggests that the verse may have already been fulfilled when the saints were driven out of the United States. But if that were the case then that would mean that the times of the Gentiles has been long fulfilled and I can’t see how anyone from that generation could have seen the desolating scourge and sickness God sends after such.
24 And this I have told you concerning Jerusalem; and when that day shall come, shall a remnant be scattered among all nations;
25 But they shall be gathered again; but they shall remain until the times of the Gentiles be fulfilled.

26 And in that day shall be heard of wars and rumors of wars, and the whole earth shall be in commotion, and men’s hearts shall fail them, and they shall say that Christ delayeth his coming until the end of the earth.
27 And the love of men shall wax cold, and iniquity shall abound.
28 And when the times of the Gentiles is come in, a light shall break forth among them that sit in darkness, and it shall be the fulness of my gospel;
29 But they receive it not; for they perceive not the light, and they turn their hearts from me because of the precepts of men.
30 And in that generation shall the times of the Gentiles be fulfilled.
31 And there shall be men standing in that generation, that shall not pass until they shall see an overflowing scourge; for a desolating sickness shall cover the land.

So the Jews will be scattered and gathered again at some point. Also, the times of the Gentiles will begin when a light breaks forth among them that sit in darkness. This light is the fulness of the gospel. This seems to be the restoration. If this is the case, the times of the Gentiles began around 1820 or 1830. I was confused about which generation it’s talking about in verse 31 but I don’t think it’s talking about the generation of the restoration in 1830 but rather the generation of the Gentiles when the Gentiles “receive it not”, referring to the fulness of the gospel. When the times of the Gentiles is fulfilled, some men of that generation will see in their lifetimes “an overflowing scourge… a desolating sickness [covering] the land.” It’s not precisely clear when the Gentiles will reach that point of rejecting that gospel but it seems possible to be now.
The maker of the  YouTube channel did a on the times of the Gentiles where he suggested that the data showing that convert baptisms have plateaued might mean that the time is now.
D&C 45:26, what does it mean that men’s hearts will fail them in the last day?
D&C 45:30-31, how could men of that generation be there at the beginning of the times of the Gentiles and at the fulfillment when it seems to span multiple generations?
In Jacob’s sermon to the Nephites after Nephi’s death he addresses their sins of pride and, for the men, sexual immorality. He states:
Jacob 2:24, 27

Behold, David and Solomon truly had many wives and concubines, which thing was abominable before me, saith the Lord. …Wherefore, my brethren, hear me, and hearken to the word of the Lord: For there shall not any man among you have save it be one wife; and concubines he shall have none;

This is pretty clear. David and Solomon having many wives and concubines was an abominable practice to God. You could maybe argue that only the concubines part was wicked but I think that’s a stretch imposing bias—it’s not how one would say that or read it normally.
Now look at a couple other scriptures:
1 Kings 15:5
Because David did that which was right in the eyes of the Lord, and turned not aside from any thing that he commanded him all the days of his life, save only in the matter of Uriah the Hittite.

37 Abraham received concubines, and they bore him children; and it was accounted unto him for righteousness, because they were given unto him, and he abode in my law; as Isaac also and Jacob did none other things than that which they were commanded; and because they did none other things than that which they were commanded, they have entered into their exaltation, according to the promises, and sit upon thrones, and are not angels but are gods.

38 David also received many wives and concubines, and also Solomon and Moses my servants, as also many others of my servants, from the beginning of creation until this time; and in nothing did they sin save in those things which they received not of me.

39 David’s wives and concubines were given unto him of me, by the hand of Nathan, my servant, and others of the prophets who had the keys of this power; and in none of these things did he sin against me save in the case of Uriah and his wife; and, therefore he hath fallen from his exaltation, and received his portion; and he shall not inherit them out of the world, for I gave them unto another, saith the Lord.

There seems to be an apparent contradiction between these accounts where it seems Jacob is saying that multiple wives and concubines are an abomination to God and D&C is saying it’s actually okay except in a few cases it describes.

Well, I found a pretty good article called . It points out verse 30 of Jacob 2 which states the exception to the rule, “For if I will, saith the Lord of Hosts, raise up seed unto me, I will command my people; otherwise they shall hearken unto these things.” This shows how if God commands multiple wives and concubines, it is acceptable to him. This is perhaps why Jacob explicitly calls out only David and Solomon and ignores the other polygamous relationships in the Bible such as those with the Patriarchs. David sinned in coveting Uriah’s wife and Solomon went unto many strange women which were not given him of God (1 Kings 11:1-6).

title: Why Have so Few Known God and His True Religion?

body.text: 1 Nephi 14:12

And it came to pass that I beheld the church of the Lamb of God, and its numbers were few, because of the wickedness and abominations of the whore who sat upon many waters; nevertheless, I beheld that the church of the Lamb, who were the saints of God, were also upon all the face of the earth; and their dominions upon the face of the earth were small, because of the wickedness of the great whore whom I saw.

Here Nephi’s vision accounts that the numbers of those who belong to the church of the Lamb are few. Why is that the case? And why does it seem to have been the case from the beginning? Why is it that the heathen nations and the unbelieving seem to have outnumbered those of God’s church from the beginning? Couldn’t God have sent more angels to minister the true religion to the world? Couldn’t He have done more?
Perhaps my questions are to God as the servant’s to the Master of the vineyard in Zenos’ allegory of the olive tree.
Jacob 5:21-22

And it came to pass that the servant said unto his master: How comest thou hither to plant this tree, or this branch of the tree? For behold, it was the poorest spot in all the land of thy vineyard. And the Lord of the vineyard said unto him: Counsel me not; I knew that it was a poor spot of ground; wherefore, I said unto thee, I have nourished it this long time, and thou beholdest that it hath brought forth much fruit.

One does wonder, though, why. Pew research provided data of the population of followers of each religion in . The results show that Christians make up almost a third of the world’s population today and Latter-day Saint membership today is just over 16 million. Of the world’s 7.9 billion people, that brings Latter-day Saints to represent only .02% of the world’s population. This is very few indeed. With some rough estimations, you can derive that the relative proportion of the world’s population that the children of Israel made up at the time when Moses led them out of Egypt was about 7.5%, or 600,000 / 80 million. Even at that time, the children of Israel made up only a small portion of the world population. Why? Couldn’t God have produced more converts? But instead, fearing that heathen nations would corrupt His covenant people—and rightfully so—he led the children of Israel to conquer instead of assimilate heathen nations.



Maybe I should back up. Perhaps my assumption that more is better is wrong. What is God’s concern? According to the allegory referenced by Zenos it seems that His concern is to produce lots of good fruit. If His garden doesn’t produce good fruit, or only produces a little bit, or if it produces bad fruit, that makes the Master of the vineyard sad and/or upset.

But what if God’s purpose with this earth and us, His people, is accomplished through a small number of us? What if quantities here are less relevant? Perhaps it’s just God’s way to work with small and simple things.
Alma 37:6

Now ye may suppose that this is foolishness in me; but behold I say unto you, that by small and simple things are great things brought to pass; and small means in many instances doth confound the wise.
Romans 12:9

And he said unto me, My grace is sufficient for thee: for my strength is made perfect in weakness. Most gladly therefore will I rather glory in my infirmities, that the power of Christ may rest upon me.

body.text: Teachings of the Prophet Joseph Smith, p. 91-92

The endowment you are so anxious about, you cannot comprehend now, nor could Gabriel explain it to the understanding of your dark minds; but strive to be prepared in your hearts, be faithful in all things, that when we meet in the solemn assembly, that is, when such as God shall name out of all the official members shall meet, we must be clean every whit. Let us be faithful and silent, brethren, and if God gives you a manifestation, keep it to yourselves; be watchful and prayerful, and you shall have a prelude of those joys that God will pour out on that day. Do not watch for iniquity in each other, if you do you will not get an endowment, for God will not bestow it on such. But if we are faithful, and live by every word that proceeds forth from the mouth of God, I will venture to prophesy that we shall get a blessing that will be worth remembering, if we should live as long as John the Revelator; our blessings will be such as we have not realized before, nor received in this generation. The order of the house of God has been, and ever will be, the same, even after Christ comes; and after the termination of the thousand years it will be the same; and we shall finally enter into the celestial kingdom of God, and enjoy it forever.

You need an endowment, brethren, in order that you may be prepared and able to overcome all things; and those that reject your testimony will be damned. The sick will be healed, the lame made to walk, the deaf to hear, and the blind to see, through your instrumentality. But let me tell you, that you will not have power, after the endowment to heal those that have not faith, nor to benefit them, for you might as well expect to benefit a devil in hell as such as are possessed of his spirit, and are willing to keep it: for they are habitations for devils, and only fit for his society. But when you are endowed and prepared to preach the Gospel to all nations, kindreds, and tongues, in their own languages, you must faithfully warn all, and bind up the testimony, and seal up the law, and the destroying angel will follow close at your heels, and exercise his tremendous mission upon the children of disobedience; and destroy the workers of iniquity, while the Saints will be gathered out from among them, and stand in holy places ready to meet the Bridegroom when he comes.

I feel disposed to speak a few words more to you, my brethren, concerning the endowment: All who are prepared, and are sufficiently pure to abide the presence of the Savior, will see Him in the solemn assembly.
The brethren expressed their gratification for the instruction I had given them. We then closed by prayer, when I returned home and retired to rest.—DHC 2:308–310.
Journal of Discourses 2:31

Your endowment is, to receive all those ordinances in the House of the Lord, which are necessary for you, after you have departed this life, to enable you to walk back to the presence of the Father, passing the angels who stand as sentinels, … and gain your eternal exaltation in spite of earth and hell.
Mosiah 2:34

I say unto you, that there are not any among you, except it be your little children that have not been taught concerning these things, but what knoweth that ye are eternally indebted to your heavenly Father, to render to him all that you have and are; and also have been taught concerning the records which contain the prophecies which have been spoken by the holy prophets, even down to the time our father, Lehi, left Jerusalem;
And behold, thou wilt remember the poor, and consecrate of thy properties for their support that which thou hast to impart unto them, with a covenant and a deed which cannot be broken.
Micah 4:13

Arise and thresh, O daughter of Zion: for I will make thine horn iron, and I will make thy hoofs brass: and thou shalt beat in pieces many people: and I will consecrate their gain unto the Lord, and their substance unto the Lord of the whole earth.

If a man come up to Zion, he must lay all things before the bishop.

It is contrary to the will and commandment of God that those who receive not their inheritance by consecration, agreeable to his law, which he has given, that he may tithe his people, to prepare them against the day of vengeance and burning, should have their names enrolled with the people of God.
Only those who receive their inheritance by consecration should have their names enrolled with the people of God.
Our Heartfelt All by Dieter F. Uchtdorf

Sacrifice and consecration are two heavenly laws that we covenant to obey in the holy temple. These two laws are similar but not identical. To sacrifice means to give something up in favor of something more valuable. Anciently, God’s people sacrificed the firstlings of their flocks in honor of the coming Messiah. Throughout history, faithful Saints have sacrificed personal desires, comforts, and even their lives for the Savior.
We all have things, large and small, we need to sacrifice in order to follow Jesus Christ more completely. Our sacrifices show what we truly value. Sacrifices are sacred and honored by the Lord.

Consecration is different from sacrifice in at least one important way. When we consecrate something, we don’t leave it to be consumed upon the altar. Rather, we put it to use in the Lord’s service. We dedicate it to Him and His holy purposes. We receive the talents that the Lord has given us and strive to increase them, manifold, to become even more helpful in building the Lord’s kingdom.
Very few of us will ever be asked to sacrifice our lives for the Savior. But we are all invited to consecrate our lives to Him.
Are there female angels—of course there are. But are there accounts of them? Do they come here and perform tasks such as the male angels who deliver messages or offer healing etc.?
Zechariah 5:9

Then lifted I up mine eyes, and looked, and, behold, there came out two women, and the wind was in their wings; for they had wings like the wings of a stork: and they lifted up the ephah between the earth and the heaven.

body.text: Was the flood sent on the earth to cleanse it from the Watchers’ wicked seed? God tells Noah (v 2) to “Hide thyself!” and “that the whole earth will be destroyed, and a deluge is about to come…” Then God talks about the wickedness of the Watchers who were fallen angels that had sexual relations with the daughters of the covenant or of man. God continues, “...destroy all the spirits of the reprobate and the children of the Watchers, because they have wronged mankind. Destroy all wrong from the face of the earth and let every evil work come to an end…” (vv. 15-16).
We understand that the flood was to rid the world of wickedness. Even the KJV says so:
Genesis 6:5
And GOD saw that the wickedness of man was great in the earth, and that every imagination of the thoughts of his heart was only evil continually.

But what if another big reason was that God saw fit to rid the world of the altered human race of seed that came from the Watchers? Such knew secrets that degenerated man according to the Book of Enoch. These secrets included the working of metals as taught by Azazel and also practices of fornication and beastiality (chapters VII - VIII). Perhaps God wanted to wipe the earth of this evil race and purify the human family.

An institute teacher from Weber State did a fireside the other day that Kaylene and I attended. His name is Brother Reed. He presented, among other things, a concept of a Tri-Messiahship belief of Judaism. To my chagrin, I couldn’t find any terminology related to this online associated with Jewish belief. Regardless, the concept is that the Jews looked forward to three messiahs: Elijah—the preparer, Elias/Messiah—the deliverer, and “that prophet”—the restorer. We interpret these to be, respectively, John the Baptist, Jesus Christ, and Joseph Smith.
John 1:20-30 (JST)
20 And this is the record of John, when the Jews sent priests and Levites from Jerusalem, to ask him; Who art thou?
21 And he confessed, and denied not that he was Elias; but confessed, saying; I am not the Christ.
22 And they asked him, saying; How then art thou Elias? And he said, I am not that Elias who was to restore all things. And they asked him, saying, Art thou that prophet? And he answered, No.
23 Then said they unto him, Who art thou? that we may give an answer to them that sent us. What sayest thou of thyself?
24 He said, I am the voice of one crying in the wilderness, Make straight the way of the Lord, as saith the prophet Esaias.
25 And they who were sent were of the Pharisees.
26 And they asked him, and said unto him; Why baptizest thou then, if thou be not the Christ, nor Elias who was to restore all things, neither that prophet?
27 John answered them, saying; I baptize with water, but there standeth one among you, whom ye know not;

28 He it is of whom I bear record. He is that prophet, even Elias, who, coming after me, is preferred before me, whose shoe’s latchet I am not worthy to unloose, or whose place I am not able to fill; for he shall baptize, not only with water, but with fire, and with the Holy Ghost.
29 The next day John seeth Jesus coming unto him, and said; Behold the Lamb of God, who taketh away the sin of the world!

30 And John bare record of him unto the people, saying, This is he of whom I said; After me cometh a man who is preferred before me; for he was before me, and I knew him, and that he should be made manifest to Israel; therefore am I come baptizing with water.

It is a little odd in verse 26 how the JST mentions the Christ, Elias, and “that prophet” as three separate beings. I thought the teaching was supposed to be that “Elias who was to restore all things” was the same as “that prophet.” Also, the JST doesn’t flow very well at the beginning of this quotation—just saying. Anyway, it’s cool because apparently Joseph Smith translated this chapter with an implied understanding of his role as the third messiah who restores things mentioned here. If he wasn’t aware of this implication then at least he translated it allowing for such an interpretation.

body.text: Adam and Eve are cast out of the garden and can’t find food for seven days. Eve asks Adam to go find food and he travels seven days in search and finds no food like what they had in paradise. Eve asks Adam if he’ll kill her since she was the reason he was driven out of the garden in the first place. Adam rebukes such an idea and reasons that God would bring another curse on them.
As they continue to search for food they can’t find paradisiacal food but only animals. Adam tells Eve that God provided animals for both animals and brutes to eat.
Very interesting side note here—are brutes early humans and sapiens?

Adam suggests that they display penitence and tells Eve to stand in the river Tigris up to her neck for thirty seven days and speak nothing since they are unworthy to address God. He says that meanwhile he’ll stand in the Jordan river up to his neck for forty days. Adam commands the living things in the water to mourn with him and they do so and swarm around and the water becomes stagnant.
Satan gets angry and transforms himself into the brightness of angels and goes to the Tigris river.

Satan deceives Eve into thinking that he is an angel visiting her in her distress and penitence. He tells her to come out of the water and partake of the food that they had in paradise. Eve comes out trembling from the cold of the water and falls on the ground. Satan picks her up and they go to Adam who recognizes the Devil and chastises Eve for interrupting her penitence.
Eve doubles her anguish after recognizing it was the Devil in disguise.

Adam then questions the Devil why he torments them when they have done nothing to him. He responds that he was cast down out of heaven because of Adam. Adam defends himself saying that he had never harmed the Devil. The Devil says that when Adam was created and given the breath of life that God told Michael to command the hosts of heaven to worship Adam. When the Devil was commanded to do so he rebelled seeing that he, himself, was more ancient than Adam and deserved Adam's worship. The angels under the Devil also rebelled when hearing the Devil's response.
Michael tells the Devil that if he doesn't worship Adam, God will be angered.

The Devil refused to worship Adam and was banished along with his host of angels. He explains how he torments Adam because he saw Adam enjoying glory in paradise while the Devil was banished and removed from his glory.

Adam laments and says "Oh Lord my God, my life is in Your hands. Banish this adversary far from me, who seeks to destroy my soul, and give me his glory which he himself has lost" (17:1). The Devil then disappears.

Adam continues his 40 days of standing on the rock in the water up to his neck in the Jordan River. Eve despairs that Adam suffers from a second error of hers and explains "I have erred and been led astray", also, "you did not commit neither the first nor the second error" (18:1). She continues, "And now banish me from the light of your life and I will go towards the sunset and stay there until I die" (18:1).

Eve walks into the west while being three months pregnant. The day approaches that her labor pains come to deliver the child of her womb. She cries out in pain and Adam can't hear her. She cries out to the Luminaries asking them to tell Adam of her pains when they rise again in the east.

But in that hour Adam knows of her pain and considers that she might be tormented by the Devil and third time. He goes to her and she tells him she is relieved of her pain at his sight. She asks him to pray and he does.
Twelve angels and two virtues appear and gather on her right and left.

Michael, the archangel, appears and puts his head on Eve's breast telling her that she will be blessed with deliverance from her pains. She bears a child and he is shining when he is born. The child immediately gets up and grabs a blade of grass. They name the child Cain.
Michael teaches Adam how to till the ground and harvest plants.

Eve has another child who they name Abel. She has a vision that distresses her where sees Cain kill Abel and is gulping his blood. Because of this vision, she and Adam separate Cain and Abel by making Cain and farmer and Abel and shepherd. Nevertheless, Cain slays Abel.

Adam and Eve conceive again and Eve bears Seth to replace Abel. Adam teaches Seth of the secrets and revelations he had. He says that when he partook of the forbidden fruit he knew God's will and the future. He tells Seth that he learned then "What God intends to do to his creation, the race of men, [in the times to come]" (29:3). Adam says God will appear in a flame of fire and give commandments and statutes and they will sanctify him. He teaches that man "will build a house to the Lord... in the land [which He shall prepare for them]" but that "they will transgress His statutes and their sanctuary will be burnt up and their land will be deserted and they themselves will be dispersed; because they... provoked the wrath of God" (29:5).

Although, "once more [in the third/seventh day] He will cause them to come back from their dispersion; and again they will build the house of God; and in the last time the house of God will be exalted greater than of old. And once more iniquity will exceed righteousness. And thereafter God will dwell with men on earth [in visible form]; and then, righteousness will begin to shine. And the house of God will be honoured in the age and their enemies will no more be able to hurt the men, who believe in God; and God will gather for Himself a faithful people, whom He shall save for eternity, and the impious shall be punished by God their king, the men who refused to love His law" (29:6-7).

Adam continues that "the just shall shine like the sun" in that day; and "men will be purified by water from their sins" (29:9). He also tells that the unwilling and unrepentant will be condemned. But the man whose soul is set right will be happy.
Adam holds a grand council with all his posterity at the age of 930 because he sees his days are coming to an end.
There are 25,000 men in the assembly, not counting women and children.

Adam declares that he is growing sick and experiencing pain. His children implore what he means by this. Seth suggests to Adam that he longs for the fruit of paradise that he used to eat. Seth offers to go to the borders of paradise and throw dust on his head and mourn and lament loudly that perhaps an angel will bring fruit for him.
Adam explains to his children that God had cursed him after partaking of the forbidden fruit with 70 curses on his body from head to toe and on every limb. He then cries out in pain.

Eve laments that Adam suffers because of her sins. She asks him to share his pain with her since she is the one who sinned. Adam asks Seth and Eve to go to the borders of paradise and lament and seek the oil of mercy to relieve him of his pain.

They journey toward the place and a serpent bites Seth. Eve blames herself because of her sins. The serpent tells her it is raged because of her. Seth rebukes the serpent and tells it to shut its mouth until judgment day and to stay away from the image of God. The serpent leaves and Seth's wound from the bite vanishes.

They go to the entrance of paradise and Michael meets them and tells them they can’t have the healing oil but that Christ would anoint all with healing oil when he died on the cross later. Instead, Michael gives them a branch from the tree of the fruit of knowledge of good and evil. They carry the tree back but accidentally drop it in the river Jordan. When they get back to Adam they tell him what had happened and he asks them to bring the branch back. Seth goes back and finds it floating in the middle of the river Jordan and the water around it is stagnant.
This part about the branch is from the Interpolations of Nicodemus and isn't part of the Latin record the rest of this book is from.

Anyway, Seth brings back the branch and Adam has them plant it at his headstone where he’s buried. The tree grows. Later, the tablets telling the account of Adam and Eves’ lives are interpreted by Solomon the wise and he finds the said tree and brings it into his kingdom. When the queen of the south visits Solomon, she inquires about the tree. The tree is then thrown into the pool of Bethesda which is troubled occasionally by an angel and takes on healing power until Christ commands someone to enter the water for the last time during His ministry.
Finally, that very tree is taken and made into the cross whereon Christ is hung and crucified.

Other interesting notes is that this record says that 5,500 years after, or near, Adam’s death at the age of 930 is said to be when “...will come the most beloved king Christ, the son of God, to revive the body of Adam and with him to revive the bodies of the dead” (xlii:2-3).

title: Review of Slavanic Life of Adam and Eve

body.text: This record is similar to the one reviewed above (the Latin translation) but with a few variations. For one, Adam admits that he had thoughts of killing Eve when they’re first cast out of the garden because she was the one who sinned and led both of them away but he forebears because God created her image and “thou showest penitence and criest to God; hence my heart hath not departed from thee” (xxxix:1).
Also, when Eve goes in the Tigris river and Adam in the Jordan to display their penitence, Eve is not fooled by the devil when he appears but identifies and ignores him.
Slavanic Life of Adam and Eve xxxix:1-2

But I (Eve) perceived that he was the devil and answered him nothing. But Adam (when) he returned from Jordan, saw the devil's footprints, and feared lest perchance he had deceived me; but when he had remarked me standing in the water he was overcome with joy (and) he took me and led me out of the water.

One other interesting part is that when Adam tells Eve to go in the Tigris river while he goes in the Jordan river he tells her “Take great care of thyself. Except thou seest me and all my tokens, depart not out of the water, nor trust in the words, which are said to thee, lest thou fall again into the snare” (xxxvi:3)

This part makes me think of Joseph Smith’s teaching of detecting evil spirits by testing their words and tokens. Perhaps Eve used this method or simply ignored all visitors despite their seemingly heavenly appearance of the “brightness of angels.”
I will explain only how this text varies from the ones above.

In this text, Eve has a dream where Cain drinks the blood of Abel and although Eve pleads that he leaves some, Cain drinks it all. He then throws up some blood. After Eve tells Adam this, they go and check on them and find that Cain had killed Abel. Because of this, Michael tells Adam, “Reveal not the secret that thou knowest to Cain thy son, for he is a son of wrath. But grieve not, for I will give thee another son in his stead; he shall show (to thee) all that thou shalt do. Do thou tell him nothing” (iii:2). This could explain why in the other record Adam tells Seth his secrets and not Cain, his firstborn. Also note that Eve also knew these secrets together with Adam.
Adam grows old and begins to suffer pain and sickness. He calls together all of his seed and Seth approaches him and asks why he is troubled. Adam responds, and I quote:
Apocalypse of Moses vii:1-ix:1

vii 1 And Adam said to him: When God made us, me and your mother, through whom also I die, He gave us power to eat of every tree which is in paradise, but, concerning that one only, He charged us not to eat of it, and through this one we are to die. And the hour drew nigh for the angels 2 who were guarding your mother to go up and worship the Lord, and I was far from her, and the enemy knew that she was alone and gave to her, and she ate of the tree of which she had been told not to eat. 3 Then she gave also to me to eat.

viii 1 'And God was wroth with us, and the Lord came into paradise and called me in a terrible voice and said: "Adam, where art thou? And why hidest thou from my face? Shall the house be able to hide itself from its builder?" And he saith to me: "Since thou hast abandoned my covenant, I have brought upon thy body seventy-two strokes; the trouble of the first stroke is a pain of the eyes, the second stroke an affection of the hearing, and likewise in turn all the strokes shall befall thee."'
ix 1 As he said this to his sons, Adam groaned sore and said: 'What shall I do? I am in great distress.

Adam suggests that Eve and Seth journey to the edge of paradise and put dung and dust on their heads and mourn so that they can receive oil from the tree of mercy to heal Adam. During their journey this happens and I thought it was short enough and interesting enough to just quote directly:
Apocalypse of Moses x-xii

x Then Seth and Eve went towards paradise, and Eve saw her son, and a wild beast assailing him, and Eve wept and said: 'Woe is me; if  I come to the day of the Resurrection, all those who have sinned will curse me saying: Eve hath not kept the commandment of God.' And she  spake to the beast: 'Thou wicked beast, fearest thou not to fight with the image of God? How was thy mouth opened? How were thy teeth made strong? How didst thou not call to mind thy subjection? For long ago wast thou made subject to the image of God.' Then the beast  cried out and said:

xi  'It is not our concern, Eve, thy greed and thy wailing, but thine own; for (it is) from thee that the rule of the beasts hath arisen. How was thy  mouth opened to eat of the tree concerning which God enjoined thee not to eat of it? On this account, our nature also hath been transformed. Now therefore thou canst not endure it,  if I begin to reprove thee.'

xii Then Seth speaketh to the beast, 'Close thy mouth and be silent and stand off from the image of God until the day of Judgment.' Then saith the beast to Seth: 'Behold, I stand off from the image of God.' And he went to his lair.
Michael appears and tells them they won’t have the oil of the tree of mercy until the last days when Christ returns and evil is no more in peoples’ hearts.

When Adam and Eve return, Adam laments toward Eve that she had brought upon them death. He tells her to bring together their seed so they can tell everyone of the nature of the transgression they made in the garden.

Eve tells the transgression story. She starts out telling how she was in the garden with her dominion which was the south and west parts of the garden with the female animals while Adam was in his dominion which was the north and east parts of the garden with the male animals.

The devil had persuaded a snake to let him use the snake to do his bidding. The next part is difficult to understand precisely, but it seems that the devil appeared as an angel singing hymns right outside the wall of paradise and Eve peered over the wall and saw him. He asked her what she was doing and she responded that she was guarding paradise as God had directed her. Following that point, the devil no longer responds via the angel of light appearance but through the snake which hung itself on the garden wall.

He tells Eve he’s disappointed that they don’t partake of all the fruit. He gets Eve to swear an oath to him that she will eat the fruit and get Adam to eat the fruit that gives knowledge of good and evil.
When the devil gives Eve the fruit he pours the poison of his wickedness—lust—on the fruit and bends the branch down to the earth so Eve can grab it. After eating, Eve accounts:
Apocalypse of Moses xx

And in that very hour my eyes were opened, and forthwith I knew that I was bare of the righteousness with which I had been clothed (upon), and I wept and said to him: "Why hast thou done this to me in that thou hast deprived me of the glory with which I was clothed?" But I wept also about the oath, which I had sworn. But he descended from the tree and vanished. And I began to seek, in my nakedness, in my part for leaves to hide my shame, but I found none, for, as soon as I had eaten, the leaves showered down from all the trees in my part, except the fig tree only. But I took leaves from it and made for myself a girdle and it was from the very same plant of which I had eaten.

Adam dies and is buried with Abel because Cain tried to bury and hide Abel’s body when he had killed him but each time the earth would bring Abel back up and say “I will not receive a companion body, till the earth which was taken and fashioned in me cometh to me” (x1:5).
So the angels took Abel’s body and left it on a rock unburied. But now the angels took Adam and Abel and put them in a tomb and sealed it until Eve died and she was put with them.

title: The Origin of The Life of Adam and Eve Texts

body.text: These texts were thought to originate in some ancient Jewish record and were translated and made into the Greek and Latin and other versions around the third-to-fifth centuries AD
The reviews of these variations can be found on the Wikipedia page.
Note on the origin of the text

This text was found in the Nag Hammadi Library which was a codex of ancient texts found in upper Egypt that date to early centuries A.D. This particular text is thought to originate from the first-to-second centuries AD.
Notes from reading

There’s a part where Adam prophecies of Noah and what will happen during his time. It’s interesting because he references a generation that scorns God after Noah and Noah swears that they didn’t descend from him. Who are these other human beings? Were they survivors of the flood or from a land which wasn’t flooded? Were they seed of women who had relations with the watchers?

Then God will rest from his wrath. And he will cast his power upon the waters, and give power to his power to his sons and their wives by means of the ark along with the animals, whichever he pleased, and the birds of heaven, which he called and released upon the earth. And God will say to Noah - whom the generations will call Deucalion - -"Behold, I have protected you in the ark along with your wife and your sons and their wives and their animals and the birds of heaven, which you called and released upon the earth.Therefore I will give the earth to you - you and your sons.In kingly fashion you will rule over it - you and your sons. And no seed will come from you of the men who will not stand in my prescense in another glory."

Then they will become as the cloud of the great light.Those men will come who have been cast forth from the knowledge of the great Aeon and the angels.They will stand before Noah and the Aeons. And God will say to Noah, "Why have you departed from what I told you? You have created another generation so that you may scorn my power" Then Noah will say , "I shall testify before your might that the generation of these men did not come from me nor from my sons."

This could be interpreted as Noah saying that this generation was not Noah’s children or grandchildren (two generations). Perhaps it could be Noah absolving himself of responsibility for their actions.

Well there’s really nothing else to say about this record. It talks about thirteen kingdoms which each describe a different way through which he comes. I’m still not even sure who “he” is. The writing is very hard to follow. I don’t think this record is very interesting.
Honestly, the Wikipedia page gives a good summary.

Adam in his 700th year tells his son Seth about how when he and Eve had first been created, they used to walk in the glory of the eternal God, and they were in fact more powerful than their creator (Yaldabaoth, the ruler of the aeons). However, that glory and knowledge was lost to them when Yaldabaoth became angry with them and divided them into two aeons (i.e. male and female). They became slaves to the creator, and also to death.  Adam then relates to Seth the hidden knowledge he received in a revelation from three mysterious men. Adam then prophesizes about attempts of the subcreator god to destroy mankind, including the prophecy of the great global flood and of attempted destruction by fire.  Adam further prophesizes that after the floodwaters have receded, God will give the earth to Noah (who will be known to posterity as Deucalion, the hero of the flood caused by Zeus in Greek mythology). Noah will then divide the earth among his sons, Ham and Japheth and Shem, with the caveat that they must always serve God "in fear and slavery". Then the descendants of Ham and Japheth (no mention is made of Shem) will form twelve kingdoms, and also be part of a thirteenth kingdom. "The illuminator of knowledge" will then come to redeem the souls of Noah's descendants.  Adam then foretells the coming of the Illuminator, who will perform miracles and pass knowledge onto Noah's descendants. The powers of God are jealous of the Illuminator, since he appears to be more powerful than they are, and they inquire about his origin. The thirteen different kingdoms each describe a different origin story for the Illuminator, each ending with the phrase "And thus he came to the water". Of these stories, only the "generation without a king," proclaims the truth.
